title: Brontosaurus excelsus — the thunder lizard
claim: Brontosaurus excelsus — the 'thunder lizard' — was a real Late Jurassic sauropod. Othniel Charles Marsh named the species in 1879 from a partial skeleton (type specimen YPM 1980) found at Como Bluff, Wyoming, during the Bone Wars. In 1903 Elmer Riggs sank Brontosaurus into Apatosaurus on the principle of taxonomic priority (Marsh had named Apatosaurus ajax first, in 1877), so the name sat unused for 112 years. In 2015, a ~300-page peer-reviewed revision of Diplodocidae (Tschopp, Mateus & Benson, PeerJ 3:e857, 7 April 2015) — 477 morphological characters scored across 81 specimens — found Brontosaurus distinct enough to stand as its own genus again, with three species: B. excelsus, B. parvus, and B. yahnahpin.
place: Como Bluff, Wyoming — type locality (Morrison Formation)
grade_reason: The animal was never in doubt: the YPM 1980 skeleton exists at the Yale Peabody Museum and every specialist from Riggs 1903 on agreed excelsus is a distinct species; the only question was which genus name to file it under, and the 2015 reinstatement is peer-reviewed, quantitative, and adopted by the Paleobiology Database and modern museum mounts.
earliest_attestation: Othniel Charles Marsh, 'Principal characters of American Jurassic dinosaurs' (1879) — Brontosaurus excelsus named from the Como Bluff skeleton

sources.ref: Marsh, O.C. (1879) — Brontosaurus excelsus named from Como Bluff skeleton; type specimen YPM 1980 (Yale Peabody Museum)

Riggs, E.S. (1903) 'Structure and Relationships of Opisthocoelian Dinosaurs, Part I: Apatosaurus Marsh', Field Columbian Museum: 'As the term Apatosaurus has priority, Brontosaurus will be regarded as a synonym'

Tschopp, E., Mateus, O. & Benson, R.B.J. (2015) 'A specimen-level phylogenetic analysis and taxonomic revision of Diplodocidae', PeerJ 3:e857, doi:10.7717/peerj.857 — 477 characters, 81 specimens; Brontosaurus reinstated with B. excelsus, B. parvus, B. yahnahpin

McIntosh, J.S. & Berman, D.S. (1975) — sorted the skull problem: Marsh's mount wore a chimeric Camarasaurus skull; Earl Douglass's 1909 skull (CM 3018) was the real one, mislabeled Diplodocus for decades until McIntosh recognized it

competing_hypotheses: The lumper position: Riggs 1903 was right and the 2015 split is oversplitting — some Morrison-taxonomy researchers (in the Taylor & Wedel line) still prefer fewer genera
Robert Bakker's 1990s position: A. excelsus always deserved its own genus — the 2015 study supplied the quantitative case he lacked
falsifiability: Proof that the YPM 1980 holotype is a chimera of unrelated taxa in a way that invalidates the species (Marsh's mounted skull was a chimera — Camarasaurus bones from three quarries — but the postcranial skeleton is a real individual, sorted by McIntosh & Berman 1975), or a peer-reviewed specimen-level analysis overturning the 2015 reinstatement

title: Dragon Man identified as Denisovan (2025 molecular work)
claim: The Harbin ('Dragon Man') cranium — a Middle Pleistocene skull with thick brow ridges, a roomy braincase, and cheeks between Neanderthal ruggedness and modern delicacy — has been identified as a Denisovan individual: mitochondrial DNA recovered from its dental calculus (maternal line) matched Denisovans from Denisova Cave, and 95 ancient proteins from the petrous bone (19,299 peptides) placed it with Denisovans at 98–100% statistical support, with three Denisovan-associated amino-acid variants (one high-confidence). After 15 years as a genome without a face, the Denisovans have a skull.
place: Harbin, Heilongjiang, China (cranium found 1933, described 2021)
grade_reason: Two independent molecular lines (mtDNA from calculus, proteomics from petrous bone) converge on the same identification, published in Cell and Science; the variant-panel caution from Xijun Ni is stated and keeps this below VERIFIED.
earliest_attestation: Fu et al., Cell, June 2025 (dental calculus mtDNA); Fu et al., Science, June 2025 (petrous-bone palaeoproteomics)

sources.ref: Fu et al. 2025, Cell (June) — mitochondrial DNA from the Harbin cranium's dental calculus identifies it as Denisovan
Fu et al. 2025, Science (June) — petrous-bone proteomics: 95 ancient proteins, 19,299 peptides, Denisovan-specific variants

Science News 2025; CNN 2025-12-26 ('How 2025 tipped the scales'); Earth.com 2025 — coverage; Bence Viola: 'pretty clear this is a Denisovan individual'; Chris Stringer on H. longi as the likely official designation
Xijun Ni (IVPP) dissent: larger ancient-protein-variant sample needed

Bianfu Cave (Yunnan, China), two Nature papers 9 Sept 2026 (doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10997-4) — five new Denisovan specimens incl. the first Denisovan forearm bone, ~167-134 ka, proteomic ID (Fu Qiaomei team); appended 2026-10-18 as grade-neutral chain-strengthening (Turin-shroud precedent): enriches the Denisovan fossil picture, does not independently confirm the Harbin ID; see evt-bianfu-cave-denisovans-2026-001

competing_hypotheses: Homo longi stands as a separate species: the original 2021 designation, now weakened — Chris Stringer notes the DNA finding makes H. longi likely the official designation for the Denisovan fossils rather than a rival taxon

The protein evidence is underpowered: Xijun Ni (IVPP) argues the sample of ancient protein variants is still too small to be definitive — the molecular face of the Denisovans rests on a narrow variant set

The mtDNA is maternal-only: in principle the Harbin individual could be a hybrid (cf. the 2018 Denisova Cave girl with a Neanderthal mother and Denisovan father) — the proteomics answers this, but the caution is on record
falsifiability: Nuclear DNA recovery from the Harbin cranium assigning it to a different lineage would overturn the identification; a larger protein-variant panel failing to group Harbin with Denisovans would weaken it to CLAIMED.

title: Birds are living theropod dinosaurs
claim: Birds are not merely descended from dinosaurs — they are theropod dinosaurs, the one dinosaur lineage to survive the K-Pg extinction. Feathered non-avian theropods (Sinosauropteryx 1996 onward, scores of Liaoning taxa, Norellraptor barsboldi 2026) plus skeletal synapomorphies (furcula, three-fingered manus, hollow thin-walled bones, semi-lunate carpal, brooding posture, air-sac pneumaticity) make the dinosaur–bird link a scientific consensus.
place: Liaoning Province, China (feathered theropod beds)
grade_reason: Multiple independent lines (feathered fossils, skeletal synapomorphies, genome-scale phylogenetics) converge; the named historical skeptic (Feduccia) holds a tiny, effectively rejected minority position.
earliest_attestation: Archaeopteryx (1861); first non-avian feathered dinosaur Sinosauropteryx (1996)

sources.ref: Archaeopteryx specimens (1861 onward) — the original dinosaur–bird bridge
Sinosauropteryx (1996) and the Liaoning feathered theropods — scores of plumage-bearing specimens
Cau, Ji, Wang et al. 2026, Nature Communications (Norellraptor barsboldi — newest feathered microraptorine, mosaic flight-feature evolution)
Feduccia, Lingham-Soliar & Hinchliffe 2005, Journal of Morphology — the prominent historical minority (BAND view); effectively rejected by subsequent evidence, stated fairly

Cau, Ji, Wang et al. 2026, Nature Communications, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-77804-6 — Norellraptor barsboldi (Jiufotang Fm, Liaoning): complete 57-cm feathered microraptorine; ~30% of the anatomical changes across microraptorine evolution also evolved in the bird lineage, but in a different order — flight-adjacent features converging independently rather than once

Xu, L., Wang, M., Lin, G. et al. 2026, Nature 658, 690-697 — Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis (Zhenghe Fauna, Fujian, ~148-150 Ma): the earliest known flightless bird — crow-sized, terrestrial, placed just above Archaeopteryx within Avialae; early bird evolution explored non-flight niches from the start — grade-neutral enrichment of the mosaic-evolution case, Turin-shroud precedent (see evt-yuezhuornis-flightless-2026-001)

Nature Communications 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-78343-w — Infernogallus jamesi, Hell Creek ~66 Ma: first nearly complete caenagnathid skull; jaw mechanics consistent with frugivory — widens the documented dietary range of feathered non-avian dinosaurs at the boundary (recorded in evt-infernogallus-jamesi-2026-001)

competing_hypotheses: The BAND view (Feduccia, Martin et al.): birds not descended from theropods; Liaoning 'protofeathers' as collagenous skin-fiber meshworks; digit-identity mismatch — a real peer-reviewed position, decisively outpaced by 14 years of new taxa, molecular preservation, and frame-shift resolution of the digit problem
Ornithoscelida (Baron et al. 2017): rearranges theropod–ornithischian relations; leaves birds inside Dinosauria either way
falsifiability: A crown-group bird fossil demonstrably predating all theropod dinosaurs, or phylogenetic evidence placing birds outside Dinosauria with support exceeding the current fossil+genomic stack

title: Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis (2026) — the runner-bird
claim: In October 2026, paleontologists described Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, a crow-sized Jurassic bird (~150 Ma) from Fujian, China, with undersized wings suggesting it was more runner than flier — complicating the paradigm that the early avian body plan evolved almost exclusively under selection for flight (Wang et al., Nature, Oct 2026).
place: Fujian Province, southeastern China
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed description of a near-complete fossil in Nature, reported by Reuters; the specimen is the exhibit, the 'runner' reading is the authors' fenced interpretation.
earliest_attestation: Wang et al. 2026, Nature (published 14 Oct 2026)

sources.ref: Wang et al. 2026, Nature (14 Oct 2026) — Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis description
Reuters (Will Dunham), 14 Oct 2026 — 'Chinese fossil of bird with undersized wings scrambles avian evolution'

competing_hypotheses: The 'runner' ecology is the describers' functional interpretation; future biomechanical work could revise it
A single specimen cannot rewrite the paradigm alone — the complication stands, the rewrite would need a series
falsifiability: Biomechanical analysis demonstrating powered-flight capability in Yuezhuornis, or re-dating outside the Late Jurassic

title: Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis — the Jurassic flightless bird
claim: A crow-sized (~800 g) avialan from the Zhenghe Fauna of Fujian, China (~148-150 Ma, Late Jurassic), described October 2026 (Xu, Wang, Lin et al., Nature 658:690-697, DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10972-z) as the earliest known bird to have lost (or diminished) the ability to fly. Forelimbs ~one-third shorter than hindlimbs; limb proportions match modern ground-dwelling birds (377 living species compared); retains dinosaurian traits — serrated teeth, hyperextensible deinonychosaur-style second toe. Placed just above Archaeopteryx within Avialae, closest relative Zhengheornis. The authors' reading: early bird evolution explored non-flight niches from the start, not a linear march toward better flight.
place: Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China — Zhenghe Fauna (approximate county coordinates)
grade_reason: Single peer-reviewed primary description in Nature (Oct 2026); independent corroboration pending. Consistent with the graded dinosaur-bird transition family; no competing published refutation.
earliest_attestation: Xu, L., Wang, M., Lin, G. et al., Nature 658, 690-697, published 14 Oct 2026

sources.ref: Xu, L., Wang, M., Lin, G. et al. 2026, Nature 658, 690-697 — 'Jurassic flightless bird reveals early ecological diversity of avialans' (nearly complete skeleton; forelimb/hindlimb ratio ~2/3; 377-living-species limb-proportion comparison; serrated teeth + hyperextensible second toe; phylogenetic placement just above Archaeopteryx within Avialae, closest relative Zhengheornis)

Reuters (Dunham), 14 Oct 2026 — Wang: 'Yuezhuornis challenges the traditional paradigm that the avian body plan evolved almost exclusively under the selective pressures of flight'; roadrunner-style runner inference stated by the authors
Xinhua, 15 Oct 2026 (via People's Daily) — IVPP + Fujian Institute of Geological Sciences provenance; earliest known example of a bird losing flight, per the describing team

Fenced nuance (diversionedge, Oct 2026, summarizing the paper): short wings do not by themselves prove flightlessness — the claim rests on limb measurements + ecological/evolutionary analysis combined; the fossil alone 'does not reveal exactly how this species' flightlessness evolved'. The ecological-diversity reading is the authors'; the terrestrial-flightless lifestyle is an inference from proportions, not preserved behavior.

competing_hypotheses: Capable of weak/short-burst flight rather than fully flightless — the authors themselves leave 'incapable of robust powered flight' open (diversionedge summary of the paper); Wang affirmed roadrunner-style short bursts as likely
Whether Yuezhuornis's lineage secondarily lost flight from flying ancestors or never achieved it — unresolved on the record
falsifiability: Overlapping new specimens showing different limb proportions, or a phylogenetic re-analysis placing Yuezhuornis outside Avialae, would sink the earliest-flightless-bird reading; additional Zhenghe avialans would test the 'ecological diversity from the start' claim.

title: Adult Sinovenator — the troodontid grows up (Ningcheng Basin, 2026)
claim: A new adult postcranial skeleton of Sinovenator changii from the Jehol Biota of the Ningcheng Basin, Inner Mongolia, described October 2026, provides the first adult ontogenetic data for this early troodontid and expands its known geographic range beyond Liaoning's Yixian Formation — refining the dinosaur–bird transition record with growth data, not just feathers.
place: Ningcheng Basin, Inner Mongolia, China (Jehol Biota)
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed description of a diagnostic adult specimen with postcranial anatomy, histological ontogeny, and range data; withheld from VERIFIED because the adult series is one data point and ontogenetic staging is method-dependent.
earliest_attestation: Described October 2026 (Yu, Zhang, Zhou & Pei, Swiss Journal of Palaeontology 145)

sources.ref: Yu, Zhang, Zhou & Pei 2026, Swiss Journal of Palaeontology 145:901–926 — 'A new postcranial skeleton of Sinovenator changii (Theropoda, Troodontidae) from the Jehol Biota of the Ningcheng Basin, Inner Mongolia, China' (postcranial anatomy, ontogeny via osteohistology, paleogeographic range)
ScienMag, 15 October 2026 — reporting the adult specimen and the expanded range of early troodontids (Jehol Biota, Ningcheng Basin, Inner Mongolia)

competing_hypotheses: The 'adult' staging rests on osteohistology — growth-ring reading is the method's known uncertainty; a re-read as late-subadult would soften the ontogenetic claim without touching the range extension
The range extension rests on one specimen — a single outlier individual versus an established Ningcheng population remains an open reading until more specimens follow
falsifiability: Re-examination reassigning the skeleton to a different troodontid taxon, or histology re-read as subadult, would downgrade the ontogeny claim; the locality itself is the range evidence and stands unless the provenance is challenged.

title: First-star imprints in a metal-poor galaxy overdensity (Li/Kakiichi et al. 2026)
claim: A metal absorber at redshift z=5.945 along the sightline to quasar SDSS J0100+2802 shows a carbon-and-silicon over-abundance pattern consistent with Population III supernova yields; the absorber sits inside a protocluster-like overdensity of 17 spectroscopically confirmed galaxies with a mean gas-phase metallicity of ~3% solar — the strongest environmental evidence yet that first-star formation and its chemical imprints lingered into the end of reionization.
place: Sightline to quasar SDSS J0100+2802 (RA ~01h00m, Dec +28°02') — the absorber at z=5.945
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed Nature Astronomy detection: JWST-mapped galaxy context (17 members, ~3% solar) plus an absorber chemistry matching Pop III faint-supernova yields; the individual first stars are still not seen — this is their imprint, fenced as such.
earliest_attestation: Li, Kakiichi, Christensen, Cai, D'Odorico, Matthee, Kashino, Bordoloi, Mackenzie, Berg, Vanni, Salvadori, Venditti, Zhang, Bosman, Bañados, Davies, Fan, Jun, Zhu et al., 'First-star imprints in a metal-poor galaxy overdensity near the end of reionization', Nature Astronomy (published 30 Sep 2026, doi:10.1038/s41550-026-02993-5)

sources.ref: Li et al. 2026, Nature Astronomy, doi:10.1038/s41550-026-02993-5 (peer-reviewed; JWST/EIGER+ASPIRE [O III] galaxy sample, quasar absorption spectroscopy, MCMC halo-occupation fit, log(M_h,min/M_sun)=10.68)
EIGER survey + ASPIRE companion program (JWST NIRCam [O III]-emitter surveys around bright z>6 quasars)
Prior z=5.945 absorber identification (pre-JWST quasar spectroscopy; the absorber's Pop III-like C/Si pattern predates the galaxy-context work)
Theoretical Pop III supernova yields (faint low-energy explosions: C-rich, Fe-poor — matching the absorber pattern and the Milky Way halo CEMP-star population)
THESAN-ZOOM simulations (prediction that Pop III star formation persists to the very end of reionization in low-density pockets)

competing_hypotheses: The C/Si pattern comes from early Population II (ordinary) enrichment rather than genuine Pop III yields — the two overlap in part of parameter space
The overdensity's metal poverty is selection geometry (sightline bias) rather than a genuinely primitive pocket
The absorber is unrelated foreground material that happens to sit at the overdensity's redshift
falsifiability: Independent JWST follow-up of the J0100+2802 field failing to reproduce the absorber's abundance pattern, or detailed modeling showing Population II yields reproduce the C/Si ratio without Pop III input, would collapse the imprint reading

title: The Guantou small-theropod footprints — mid-Cretaceous Jialingpus trackways, Dongyang, Zhejiang, published 2026
claim: On 20 October 2026, a peer-reviewed paper in MDPI Fossils (2026, 4(4), 30) described newly discovered small theropod footprints from collapsed rock blocks of the Lower Cretaceous Guantou Formation at the Shangantian tracksite, Dongyang City, Zhejiang Province, eastern China: at least 18 natural molds on a single siltstone slab, minute tridactyl tracks 6.8–8.8 cm long, tentatively assigned to Jialingpus isp., with three single-step trackways indicating slow walking speeds of 0.4–0.8 m/s (1.4–2.9 km/h) — enriching mid-Cretaceous dinosaur track diversity in Zhejiang and informing Jialingpus morphometric variation across the Jurassic–Cretaceous boundary.
place: Shangantian tracksite, Dongyang City, Zhejiang Province, China
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed published find (MDPI Fossils, 20 Oct 2026), 18+ natural molds on one slab, measured morphometrics, tentative ichnotaxonomic assignment openly fenced by the authors; withheld from VERIFIED because the assignment is tentative and the material is collapsed-block, not in-situ.
earliest_attestation: MDPI Fossils 2026, 4(4), 30 — 'Small Theropod Footprints from the Lower Cretaceous Guantou Formation of Dongyang City, Zhejiang Province, China' — published 20 October 2026 (Feature Paper; authors at China University of Geosciences, Dinosaur Odyssey Science Museum, Zhejiang Geological Museum).

sources.ref: MDPI Fossils 2026, 4(4), 30 — 'Small Theropod Footprints from the Lower Cretaceous Guantou Formation of Dongyang City, Zhejiang Province, China' — published 20 October 2026; 13 pages; ≥18 natural molds, 6.8–8.8 cm tridactyl tracks, tentatively Jialingpus isp., 0.4–0.8 m/s walking speeds

competing_hypotheses: The Jialingpus isp. assignment is explicitly tentative in the paper — reduced mesaxony and incomplete medial metatarsophalangeal expression are read as morphometric/preservation-driven variation; a different ichnotaxonomic reading remains possible
The tracks come from collapsed blocks derived from the Guantou Formation, not in-situ quarry walls — the formation-level age is not a track-level date
falsifiability: A re-description re-identifying the molds as non-dinosaurian trace features or a different ichnotaxon would revise the Jialingpus reading; the described assemblage itself stands on the peer-reviewed print.

title: Invictibellatrix amberina — Europe's first megaraptoran
claim: A new megaraptoran theropod species, described October 2026 from a partial braincase collected on the Isle of Wight and held unstudied at the Natural History Museum, London since 1924, is the first confirmed European member of the Megaraptora — a group of large-armed, long-clawed theropods previously known from Asia and the southern continents — and its placement supports the Asia→Europe→Gondwana dispersal route over southern island-hopping.
place: Isle of Wight, UK — southwest coast, Wessex Formation (found at the foot of a cliff by R. W. Hooley)
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed species description with CT endocast evidence, a stated unique character combination, and consistent phylogenetic placement in Megaraptora; withheld from VERIFIED because the taxon rests on one partial specimen and awaits independent replication.
earliest_attestation: The fossil itself — collected c. 1920s at the foot of a southwest-coast cliff by amateur paleontologist Reginald Walter Hooley; acquired by the Natural History Museum, London, 1924; described in print October 2026

sources.ref: Morrison, Scherer, Barrett et al. 2026, Royal Society Open Science 13(10):260937 — 'A new megaraptoran dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous Wessex Formation, UK, and its implications for theropod evolution and biogeography' (CT scan, 3D endocast, phylogenetic algorithms; the oval spinal-cord foramen + hourglass-shaped crest diagnosis)

Phys.org, 13 October 2026 — 'Isle of Wight fossil Europe's first known long-clawed megaraptoran dinosaur' (UCL/NHM reporting: 3–4 m long, ~1.5 m tall, claws 10–20 cm, hyena-like ecological role; Europe→Gondwana route inference; northern Laurasian extinction modeled, cause unexplained)

New Scientist, 14 October 2026 — 'Dinosaur named new species 102 years after fossil found on Isle of Wight' (nearest comparative match: Murusraptor, ~80 Ma Argentina; no overlapping material with the similar-sized Wessex theropod Eotyrannus)

competing_hypotheses: The braincase belongs to Eotyrannus, a similar-sized Wessex Formation theropod — untestable directly: no overlapping fossil material exists between the two individuals
The Europe→Gondwana overland dispersal route is one biogeographic model; a single European specimen strengthens it but does not rule out southern island-hopping for other megaraptoran lineages
The feathered, hyena-role ecology (3–4 m, 10–20 cm claws) is inferred from relatives and allometry, not preserved in the specimen — the animal's soft tissues and behavior are reconstructions
falsifiability: A re-examination placing the braincase in Eotyrannus or another described taxon, or overlapping new specimens contradicting the megaraptoran placement, would sink the species hypothesis; the 'first European megaraptoran' claim dies the moment an older confirmed European specimen is published.

title: The Udon Thani trackway — Thailand's first Udon Thani dinosaur footprints, announced 2026
claim: On 20 October 2026, Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources announced that six tridactyl impressions exposed in sandstone of the Phu Phan Formation inside Phu Hin Chom That–Phu Phrabat National Park, Udon Thani province, are genuine dinosaur footprints — a single trackway, each print ~29 cm long and ~26 cm wide, attributed by the agency to a carnivorous theropod (~120 Ma, Early Cretaceous), estimated ~1.42 m at the hip and ~6.3 m long, comparable in build to Siamotyrannus isanensis. The site was first noticed by a tourist's photograph posted to Facebook on 18 October 2026; park rangers measured the impressions on 19 October.
place: Phu Hin Chom That–Phu Phrabat National Park, Kut Chap District, Udon Thani Province, Thailand
grade_reason: Announced and measured by Thailand's national geological agency (a primary institutional witness), not a content farm: six impressions, single trackway, documented dimensions; withheld from VERIFIED because no peer-reviewed description exists yet and the trackmaker/age readings are preliminary.
earliest_attestation: Thailand's Department of Mineral Resources announcement, 20 October 2026 (via the department's official Facebook page); the discoverer is tourist Pichai Prathetsena, whose 18 October 2026 photograph in the 'What Animal Is This?' Facebook group prompted the ranger inspection of 19 October.

sources.ref: Department of Mineral Resources (Thailand) announcement, 20 October 2026 — six tridactyl footprints, single trackway, Phu Phan Formation sandstone; 29 × 26 cm; ~1.42 m hip height, ~6.3 m length; Early Cretaceous theropod (as reported in the Oct-21 press cycle)
Wochenblitz English, 2026-10-21 — tourist Pichai Prathetsena's 18 October 2026 photograph, ranger inspection 19 October, agency confirmation 20 October; Udon Thani's first dinosaur tracks

competing_hypotheses: The Siamotyrannus-affinity reading is a size-based preliminary comparison by the agency, not a peer-reviewed taxonomic assignment — the trackmaker identity is open
The ~120 Ma age rests on the Phu Phan Formation assignment; formation-level dating is not track-level dating
Misidentification risk is low given the tridactyl morphology and sandstone trackway context, but the record honestly notes the find is announced, not yet described in peer-reviewed print
falsifiability: A peer-reviewed ichnological description re-identifying the impressions as non-dinosaurian (erosion features, pseudo-fossils) would overturn the agency's reading; the trackway's existence stands on the agency's measured field report.

title: The Paluxy 'man tracks'
claim: Fossil human footprints ('giant man tracks') occur alongside dinosaur tracks in the Cretaceous limestone of the Paluxy River near Glen Rose, Texas, proving humans and dinosaurs walked the same riverbed at the same time.
place: Paluxy River, Glen Rose, Texas (Dinosaur Valley State Park area)
grade_reason: Cleaned and mapped, the alleged 'human' prints are elongate metatarsal dinosaur tracks, erosional features, or carved blocks (Kuban's multi-year field study); even the ICR's John Morris conceded in 1986 that none of the Taylor-site trails 'can be today regarded as unquestionably human,' and Films for Christ withdrew the 'Footprints in Stone' film.
earliest_attestation: Stanley Taylor's research and film at the Paluxy sites, late 1960s–early 1970s (Taylor, 1973), building on earlier creationist claims from the 1930s–1940s

sources.ref: Glen J. Kuban, Paluxy Dinosaur / 'Man Track' controversy (paleo.cc/paluxy) — the field-work summary: all alleged 'human' prints attributed; 'I have concluded that no genuine human tracks have been found in the Paluxy riverbed'

NCSE, 'A Summary of the Taylor Site Evidence' — Morris 1986 ICR Impact article: none of the four Taylor-site trails can 'be today regarded as unquestionably human'; Films for Christ withdrew Footprints in Stone (Taylor, 1985)
Wilford, J. N. 1986, 'Fossils of Man Tracks Shown to Be Dinosaurian,' The New York Times, 17 June 1986
Hastings, R. J. 1988, 'The Rise and Fall of the Paluxy Mantracks,' Perspectives on Science and Christian Faith (American Scientific Affiliation)

doesgodexist.today (John Clayton's old-earth creationist ministry), 'Acrocanthosaurus Tracks in Glen Rose, Texas' — site visits to Dinosaur Valley State Park and Jake McFall's ranch: 'The dinosaur tracks are very clear, but the human tracks are what today we would call "fake news."' — the young-earth telling rejected by an old-earth creationist venue, i.e. a hostile witness to the claim (page updated ~Sep 2026, drought-exposed trackways all Acrocanthosaurus, 113 Ma)

competing_hypotheses: The original young-earth reading: genuine human prints in Cretaceous rock, still promoted by a few holdouts (Baugh, Patton, Juby) — not considered credible by either mainstream scientists or the major creationist groups
Kuban's reading: the majority are elongate metatarsal dinosaur tracks whose digit impressions were subdued by infilling, mud-collapse, or erosion; others are erosional features or carved blocks

The Burdick-print line: several 'man tracks' on loose blocks (including the Burdick Print) show carving evidence — subsurface features truncating at the print surface, anatomically wrong proportions, and algal-fossil orientation showing the carver worked the wrong face
falsifiability: A Paluxy print with verified human-specific anatomy — a true heel-to-toe human gait with human metrical proportions, documented in situ in the limestone bed — would reopen the case. The existing specimens have been cleaned, mapped, and attributed; none qualifies.

title: Denny — the first-generation Neanderthal/Denisovan hybrid (~90 ka)
claim: Denisova 11 ('Denny'), ~90,000 years old from Denisova Cave: nuclear genome ~38.6% Neanderthal / 42.3% Denisovan; maternally Neanderthal (mtDNA). A first-generation hybrid of a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father — the father himself carried Neanderthal ancestry 300-600 generations earlier, implying interbreeding was common, not rare.
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed ancient-DNA analysis; first-generation hybrid status follows from the 50/50 split and maternal mtDNA
earliest_attestation: Slon et al., Nature 2018
competing_hypotheses: A single hybrid could in principle be a rare event; the father's deeper Neanderthal ancestry argues against rarity
falsifiability: Additional archaic genomes could show hybrids are rare after all

title: The Youngest Toba Tuff (~74 ka) — the dated catastrophe
claim: The Youngest Toba Tuff — a super-eruption in northern Sumatra, Indonesia, dated 73.88 ± 0.32 ka (Storey et al. 2012, 40Ar/39Ar) — the largest explosive volcanic eruption of the Quaternary (VEI 8; thousands of cubic kilometres of magma). It left a caldera lake ~100 km long, laid a dated ash isochron from the Indian Ocean to the South China Sea and across South Asia, and left sulfate and cryptotephra fingerprints in both Greenland (GISP2) and Antarctic ice cores. It happened inside the Homo sapiens dispersal window — a catastrophe with a date, not a cause of one.
place: Lake Toba caldera, northern Sumatra, Indonesia
grade_reason: Multiple independent primary lines: the caldera itself, the chemically-fingerprinted distal ash blanket, and polar ice-core sulfate/cryptotephra — the best-dated supervolcanic eruption of the Quaternary.
earliest_attestation: The eruption itself — Lake Toba caldera (lat 2.6845, lon 98.8756); the ash isochron recorded in marine, terrestrial, and ice archives worldwide

sources.ref: Storey et al. 2012, 40Ar/39Ar geochronology: the Youngest Toba Tuff at 73.88 ± 0.32 ka — the standing reference age
Lake Toba caldera, northern Sumatra — the eruption's own scar: ~100 km × 30 km collapse structure
GISP2 ice core, Greenland: the ~74 ka sulfate spike attributed to Toba (Zielinski & Mershon 1997; Williams et al. 2009)
Smith et al. 2018 (and Svensson et al. 2013): cryptotephra ties between polar ice and the Toba system — the fingerprint in both hemispheres
The Youngest Toba Tuff isochron: distal ash beds across South Asia (Jwalapuram locality C, India) to the South China Sea — one layer, one date, everywhere at once

competing_hypotheses: The Greenland linkage: whether the ~74 ka GISP2 sulfate spike belongs to Toba — the cryptotephra work (Smith et al. 2018; Svensson et al. 2013) strengthens the tie, but polar attribution of any single eruption remains harder than the terrestrial ash
The two-eruption question: whether all Youngest Toba Tuff deposits come from one event or a tight sequence — the isochron reading is one-event, with revision possible
falsifiability: An independent redating that moves the Youngest Toba Tuff outside ~74 ± 2 ka; a better-candidate eruption for the global isochron; geochemical re-assignment of the distal ashes

title: The main out-of-Africa dispersal, ~50-70 ka
claim: All living non-African human populations descend from a single main dispersal of Homo sapiens out of Africa ~50-70 thousand years ago; earlier exits (Misliya ~180 ka, Apidima ~210 ka, Zhirendong, Tam Pa Ling) left fossils and tools but no surviving genetic legacy. The Sahul landmass (Australia/New Guinea) was settled ~60-65 ka via two routes (a southern corridor through Indonesia and a northern corridor toward the Philippines/New Guinea), crossing open water by boat.
place: Bab al Mandab strait, Red Sea (the southern exit); exit routes also northern (Sinai/Levant)
grade_reason: Three independent lines converge: coalescent genetics (the deepest non-African splits sit inside the 70-50 ka window, no surviving earlier contribution), archaeology (Sahul sealed ~65-60 ka with two mtDNA routes, Richards team), and the fossil exits (Misliya/Apidima/Zhirendong pre-date the window with no genetic continuity). The failed-exit catalogue is fossil-solid; the ancestry claim rests on the genetic null.
earliest_attestation: N/A (paleogenomic/archaeological reconstruction, not a text)

sources.ref: Mallick et al. 2016, Nature 538:201-206 (Simons Genome Diversity Project) — divergence dating of the out-of-Africa bottleneck
Hershkovitz et al. 2018, Science 359:456-459 — Misliya maxilla, ~177-194 ka, earliest Levantine sapiens
Harvati et al. 2019, Nature 571:500-504 — Apidima 1, ~210 ka, earliest known sapiens outside Africa
Clarkson et al. 2017, Nature 547:306-310 — Madjedbebe, Sahul occupation by ~65 ka
Richards team mtDNA/Y-chromosome/genome-wide Sahul study (archaeologymag Dec 2025 secondary coverage) — two-route arrival, no earlier than ~60 ka, oldest unbroken non-African lineages
wsws.io Sept 11, 2026 — TRACE program: two intra-African ghost lineages inferred from genomes (fenced: secondary coverage only, primary paper unverified)
IFLScience Feb 2026 — Dhofar Oman ~109-95 ka Nubian Levallois (fenced: unreviewed preprint, held in competing hypotheses)

Zhang, Biddanda, Moorjani et al. 2026, Science (doi:10.1126/science.aef8874) — the TRACE twin-ghost paper; appended 2026-10-18 (grade-neutral, Turin-shroud precedent): the ~800 ka ghost is intra-African introgression into the dispersing population, not a competing exit

competing_hypotheses: Earlier exits contributed lasting ancestry — tested and not found: the Richards mtDNA/Y-chromosome/genome-wide analysis argues the pre-50 ka dispersals left no substantial legacy in present-day populations
The northern vs southern Sahul route emphasis — the two-route reading is the current convergence; the split point (South/SE Asia) and relative timing remain modeled
The unreviewed Dhofar (Oman) ~109-95 ka Nubian Levallois study (IFLScience Feb 2026, preprint only) — if it survives peer review it extends the failed-exits catalog, not the main wave

Intra-African ghost-lineage admixture (TRACE program) — UPGRADED 2026-10-18: the primary paper is now verified and on the record (evt-trace-ghost-lineages-2026-001: Zhang, Biddanda, Moorjani et al., Science 30 July 2026, doi:10.1126/science.aef8874). The finding strengthens the dispersal record rather than challenging it: the ~800 ka ghost introgressed into the African sapiens population BEFORE the final exit, so it traveled out with the dispersers — it is not an earlier exit contributing separately. The lineage's identity stays fenced as unattested.
Coastal-first vs interior-corridor main routes — Green Sahara humid windows vs southern-coast lithic trails; both directions evidenced, neither exclusive
falsifiability: A pre-50 ka fossil with surviving DNA clustering inside a living non-African haplogroup, or ancient DNA from Misliya/Apidima-grade material showing continuity to present populations, would break the single-main-wave reading.

title: Madjedbebe — Australia's 65,000-Year Story
claim: Humans occupied the Madjedbebe rock shelter in northern Australia (Kakadu) by about 65,000 years ago — the earliest known human presence in Australia — arriving by sea voyage from Sunda, alongside megafauna and within sight of Homo floresiensis on Flores.
place: Madjedbebe rock shelter, Kakadu, Northern Territory, Australia
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed primary publication with optical dating and stratigraphic refits; the 50 ka floor is long-accepted. Held at CORROBORATED (not VERIFIED) because the 65 ka re-dating carries named expert skepticism and the OSL debate is unresolved.
earliest_attestation: Clarkson, Jacobs, Marwick et al., 'Human occupation of northern Australia by 65,000 years ago', Nature 547:306-310 (2017) — optical dating, artefact refits, three dense occupation bands.

sources.ref: Clarkson et al., Nature 547:306-310 (2017), doi:10.1038/nature22968 — 10,000+ artefacts in the lowest dense layer: world's oldest ground-edge axe technology, Australia's oldest seed-grinding tools, ochre processing, thylacine jaw with pigment

Science News 2017 — 'When people think about our ancient ancestors, they either tend to have a view that our ancestors must have been primitive... This indicates the latter view' (Peter Hiscock, Univ. of Sydney)

Madjedbebe site record — the 65 ka dating 'questioned by some experts' as of 2017; the 50 ka figure 'widely accepted since the 1990s'; excavated with custodianship of the Gundjeihmi Aboriginal Corporation

competing_hypotheses: The pre-2017 consensus of ~50 ka arrival — still the broadly accepted floor; Madjedbebe's contribution is the 65 ka extension, which is the contested part.
Media-level 80,000-year claims (Bradshaw Foundation coverage of 2017 press) — reported as press-adjacent, not peer-reviewed consensus.
falsifiability: Demonstration of sediment disturbance invalidating the OSL dates, or a replicate excavation showing the artefacts are younger, would downgrade the record.

title: Penghu 2 & 3: leg bones attributed to Denisovans by collagen proteomics (2026 preprints)

Yoneda et al., bioRxiv 8 Aug 2026, doi:10.64898/2026.08.07.743455 — collagen proteomic attribution of Penghu 3 (tibia)

The stature estimates are inflated by fragmentary extrapolation (the phys.org caution)
Penghu 1 (the 2025 mandible) was the secure Denisovan; 2/3 remain provisional

title: The September 2026 '40,000 BCE Great Pyramid' press telling
claim: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built c. 40,000 BCE — millennia before the pharaohs — as reported in a September 2026 press telling (dailygalaxy, 2026-09-10) based on an engineer's weathering measurements of the pyramid's stone.
place: Giza Plateau, Egypt
grade_reason: The claim dies on the radiocarbon: mortar charcoal dates the construction to the 4th-millennium BCE horizon, and the ceramic-sequence, graffiti, and inscription lines converge independently on Khufu's reign. A single press-reported weathering comparison with an unverified equivalence assumption cannot stand against four independent dating lines. 2026 evidence state: no peer-reviewed rebuttal published as of October 2026 (only skeptical journalism — the preprint itself was never peer-reviewed, uploaded to ResearchGate January 2026); the grade rests on the radiocarbon and convergence lines, unchanged.
earliest_attestation: The September 2026 press report; no peer-reviewed publication of the weathering measurements is cited in the reporting.

sources.ref: dailygalaxy.com 2026-09-10: 'Far Older Than Khufu: Egypt's Great Pyramid May Have Been Built in the Stone Age, as Early as 40,000 BC' — the press telling, which also carries the mainstream rebuttal (Lehner on the 3,000-year material-culture sequence; Higham on radiocarbon calibration)
Bonani, G. et al. 2001 — radiocarbon dating of pyramid mortar charcoal (the dating line the claim must defeat)

ecoticias, February 2026 — methodological gaps in the REM preprint: Egypt's climate was not constant over tens of millennia, modern pollution/acid rain accelerates erosion, shifting sand may have shielded blocks, base-level tourist foot traffic confounds the wear signal (skeptical journalism, not a formal rebuttal)

competing_hypotheses: The weathering-measurement approach: comparing surface weathering across pyramid surfaces could, in principle, detect differential age — but the report itself concedes the key assumption (that the compared surfaces are equivalent in composition and condition) has not been independently verified

The mainstream dating case: radiocarbon of mortar charcoal (Bonani et al. 2001) places construction c. 2850–2600 BCE; the pottery at Giza matches the ceramic styles of the reigns of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure (Lehner); workers' graffiti inside the pyramid names Khufu's work crews; quarry and tomb inscriptions attribute the project to Khufu's Fourth Dynasty; Higham's calibration work ties the chronology to precisely dated material (e.g., Djoser's Saqqara)
The weather-erosion tradition: Sphinx water-erosion hypotheses (Schoch, 1990s) argue for older origins, but have not displaced the radiocarbon and ceramic evidence for the pyramid's age
falsifiability: A peer-reviewed, independently replicated weathering-dating method with published methodology, plus a published answer to the radiocarbon evidence, would reopen the question. The current record rests on one press report of one engineer's measurements with an unverified core assumption.

title: Peopling of the Americas: three lines converge on 14–20 ka, reviewed 2026-10-17 (VIII.c third pass)
claim: Three independent lines of evidence — ancient-DNA population-split timing, the archaeological site record, and environmental/ice-sheet data — converge on a 14,000–20,000-year-ago window for the arrival of the ancestors of today's Indigenous Americans, per Potter et al. 2026 (Current Opinion in Genetics & Development). The genetic data show a major branching event around 15 ka dividing Northern and Southern Native American lineages; post-14-ka arrival conflicts with the split timing; pre-25-ka arrival finds no genomic population-split support. This is the convergence argument's fifth demonstration case: genetics, archaeology, and paleoenvironment sharing no method, landing in the same window.
place: North America (continental)
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed 2026 synthesis explicitly testing three migration models against three independent evidence lines; the convergence pattern (not the terminal date) is the graded claim.
earliest_attestation: Bethany Potter et al., 'Genomic insights regarding early migrations into the Americas', Current Opinion in Genetics & Development (2026), DOI: 10.1016/j.gde.2026.102534 — reported 5 Oct 2026

sources.ref: Potter et al. 2026, 'Genomic insights regarding early migrations into the Americas', Current Opinion in Genetics & Development, DOI: 10.1016/j.gde.2026.102534
phys.org / Science X Network report, 5 Oct 2026 (fact-checked; summarizes the review's three-line test of the three migration models)

The DNA clock itself: population-split dates are model-dependent; the environmental line (ice-sheet blockage) is the independent anchor

title: Atlantis (Plato's account)
claim: That Atlantis — a vast maritime empire 'beyond the Pillars of Hercules' with a concentric-ringed capital city, founded by Poseidon's descendants and destroyed in a single day and night — was a real historical place, as Plato describes it in the Timaeus and Critias (c. 360 BCE).
place: Claimed: beyond the Pillars of Hercules (Strait of Gibraltar) — no physical site
grade_reason: No independent attestation of any detail; the internal 9600 BCE chronology is impossible; no site of any age matches the described city.
earliest_attestation: Plato's Timaeus and Critias, c. 360 BCE — and no earlier source, and no independent ancient source at all. Plato is the only known ancient record of its existence.

sources.ref: Plato, Timaeus 23e–25d
Plato, Critias 108e–121c
Chapman University Survey of American Fears 2018: 56.9% agree/strongly agree that 'ancient, advanced civilizations, such as Atlantis, once existed' (belief data, not evidence)

competing_hypotheses: The scholarly consensus: Atlantis is Plato's philosophical allegory — a foil for his ideal Athens, constructed to illustrate a political-philosophical point
Marinatos 1939: a distorted cultural memory of the Theran eruption and Minoan collapse — a possible inspiration, not a verification (evt-thera-eruption-001)
The Galanopoulos/Bacon variant: Crete/Thera with a transcription error (9,000 years for 900 years, stades scaled down) — saves the story only by rewriting Plato's numbers
The literalist reading: Atlantis is still unfound (Antarctica, Azores, Richat, etc.) — each proposed site contradicts the geology, the chronology, or the description
falsifiability: A dated, in-context site matching the described capital (concentric rings, central Poseidon temple, orichalcum-working, Plato's dimensions) at Plato's location and within an order of magnitude of Plato's era.

title: Kuk Swamp — Independent Agriculture in the New Guinea Highlands
claim: People in the Wahgi Valley of the New Guinea highlands were practicing agriculture by about 10,000 years ago — planting taro and banana on the Kuk Swamp wetland margin — independently of any Near Eastern farming tradition.
place: Kuk Swamp, Wahgi Valley, Papua New Guinea Highlands
grade_reason: Multiply attested: phytolith and starch-grain residue evidence, phase-sequence stratigraphy, a former skeptic's published conversion, and a UNESCO inscription naming the independence inference explicitly. Stops short of VERIFIED on the exact domestication-vs-intensive-management reading of the 10 ka phase.
earliest_attestation: Denham et al., Science 302:189-193 (2003) — banana phytoliths, taro starch grains on stone-tool edges, ditch-margin planting in phase I.

sources.ref: Denham, Haberle et al., 'Origins of agriculture at Kuk Swamp in the highlands of New Guinea', Science 302:189-193 (2003) — phase I planting 10,220-9,910 cal BP; phases II (6,950-6,440 cal BP mounds) and III (4,350-3,980 cal BP ditch networks)

Fullagar, Field, Denham & Lentfer, 'Early and mid Holocene tool-use and processing of taro (Colocasia esculenta), yam (Dioscorea sp.) and other plants at Kuk Swamp' (2006) — starch on tool edges, processing from at least 10,200 cal BP

competing_hypotheses: The early-Holocene phase as intensive plant exploitation/management rather than full domestication — the domestication-process debate; carried honestly inside the record.
UNESCO's conservative position: unambiguous agriculture 'around 7,000-6,400 years ago' with the 10,000 BP genesis as the evidence-supported tail — not a rival, a confidence statement.
falsifiability: Re-dating of the phase-I palaeosurface to significantly younger ages, or demonstration that the residues are wild-plant processing unrelated to cultivation, would weaken the independence claim.

title: The Black Sea deluge hypothesis
claim: The Black Sea deluge hypothesis (Ryan & Pitman, 1997, Columbia University): as the last ice age waned, rising Mediterranean waters breached the Bosphorus Sill ~9,400 years ago, catastrophically flooding the then-freshwater Black Lake — drowning ~70,000 km² of Neolithic shoreline and possibly seeding the flood memories behind the Mesopotamian and Genesis stories. Giosan et al. (Quaternary Science Reviews, Jan 2009) counter that the rise was only 5-10 m, drowning ~2,000 km² — 'hardly of biblical proportions.' The hypothesis is unresolved: the reconnection happened; its catastrophic character and any link to flood traditions remain contested.
place: Black Sea basin / Bosphorus Sill
grade_reason: A real geological event (the Black Sea-Mediterranean reconnection) underlies it, but the catastrophic scale and the flood-myth link are both unresolved hypotheses, not demonstrated. SPECULATION until the coring settles the scale.
earliest_attestation: W.B.F. Ryan & W.C. Pitman III, Noah's Flood: The New Scientific Discoveries About the Event That Changed History (1998)

sources.ref: Ryan & Pitman, Noah's Flood (1998); Ryan et al., Marine Geology 138 (1997)
Giosan, Filip & Constantinescu, Quaternary Science Reviews 28 (Jan 2009)

competing_hypotheses: Catastrophic breach: Ryan & Pitman 1997 — 50-60 m rise, 70,000 km² drowned
Gradual/no catastrophic flood: Giosan et al. 2009 — 5-10 m rise, ~2,000 km²; sill overflow was gradual
Any-link-to-flood-myths: untestable without transmission evidence (most archaeologists skeptical)
falsifiability: Better Black Sea paleo-shoreline reconstruction (multibeam + coring) could settle the breach's scale; a dated Neolithic drowned-site horizon could support the catastrophic reading

title: The 'Chinchorro mummy has the oldest tattoos' myth (DEBUNKED)
claim: The world's oldest tattoos belong to a Chinchorro mummy from South America, dated to around 6000 BCE — older than Ötzi the Iceman.
place: Coastal Chile/Peru (Chinchorro culture region)
grade_reason: DEBUNKED by radiocarbon re-analysis. The Chinchorro mummy Mo-1 T28 C22 — bearing a delicate dot-mustache tattoo on the upper lip — was reported as ~6000 BP, apparently older than Ötzi. The reexamination showed the date 3830 ± 100 radiocarbon years BP (from lung tissue) had been misread as 3830 ± 100 years BC, then transposed to 5780 BP to match Allison's 'ca. 6000 BP' — and later sources pushed it further to '6000 BC' (effectively 8000 BP), some 4,000 years earlier than the actual date. The corrected comparison 'clearly identifies Ötzi as the oldest tattooed human remains discovered to date, antedating the Chinchorro mummy Mo-1 T28 C22 by at least 500 years.' The Chinchorro dot-mustache remains a genuine early tattoo — ornamental, unlike Ötzi's therapeutic lines — but it is not the oldest.
earliest_attestation: Popular and scholarly sources, pre-2015 (citing Allison 1996 and derivatives)

sources.ref: Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports (via HAL): the misreading of 3830 ± 100 BP as 3830 BC; the transposition to 5780 BP; the '6000 BC' inflation; Ötzi antedating Mo-1 T28 C22 'by at least 500 years.'
Hyperallergic: the Chinchorro dot-mustache contender; the radiocarbon comparison 'clearly identifies Ötzi as the oldest tattooed human remains discovered to date.'
RedOrbit: the reported 4000–6000 BC age range for the Chinchorro mummy; the 4,000-year dating error.

falsifiability: Corrected radiocarbon dating of the Chinchorro specimen

title: The Persian Gulf's retreating head — Eridu and Ur on a coast that left
claim: In the early Holocene the head of the Persian Gulf stood far north of its present position: c. 5000 BP the shoreline lay near Eridu and Ur (Tell el-Muqayyar), on the evidence of Larsen & Evans 1978, Lambeck 1996, and Sanlaville 1989 as synthesized in the geoarchaeological literature. The Gulf then retreated south as the Tigris-Euphrates delta prograded, reaching its current configuration c. AD 1000 via the Shatt al-Arab delta's growth south of Basra (Al-Hamad et al. 2017; Aqrawi 2001; Bogemans et al. 2017). The exact position of the shoreline at 6000 BP is still debated — Jotheri et al. 2018's remote-sensing work in the Uruk region finds the marine transgression never reached the Uruk area (~300 km from the present shoreline).
place: Head of the Persian Gulf, southern Iraq — the migrating Holocene shoreline
grade_reason: Multi-team, multi-method convergence (sea-level curves, marine-shell radiocarbon, delta-progradation chronology) on the retreating-Gulf picture; the Uruk-reach and exact-6000-BP-position disputes are stated in the record, not hidden.
earliest_attestation: Larsen & Evans 1978 (the modern literature baseline for the northern Gulf-head model).

sources.ref: Jotheri, Allen, et al. 2018 — Holocene fluvial and anthropogenic processes in the region of Uruk

Iacobucci et al. 2022 (Geomorphology, Rome) — geomorphology of the lower Mesopotamian plain at Tell Zurghul (synthesis of the Gulf-head debate: Aqrawi & Evans 1994; Altaweel 2019; Al-Hamad et al. 2017; Aqrawi 2001; Bogemans et al. 2017)
Lagash Archaeological Project (UPenn) — Ubaid settlements in estuarine marshes/along the Gulf coast; sea withdrawal then regularized Tigris-Euphrates courses

Giosan & Goodman, PLOS ONE (2025) — 'Morphodynamic Foundations of Sumer': high-resolution satellite mapping + a 25-meter sediment core from Lagash reconstructing the vanished early-Sumerian coastline; tidal-dynamics model of the head-of-Gulf estuarine world (daily tides irrigating the land) — the substrate moving inside the argument's own demonstration zone (Lagash Archaeological Project, Iraqi/Penn Museum)

competing_hypotheses: Pournelle 2003-style maximalist transgression (shoreline near Uruk c. 4000 BCE) — finds no marine signature at Uruk in the 2018 remote-sensing work
A faster or slower progradation chronology — the c. AD 1000 current-configuration date is the Al-Hamad/Aqrawi/Bogemans consensus, not a directly dated event
falsifiability: A published, dated marine deposit from the Uruk area c. 4000 BCE would restore the maximalist model; a redated progradation sequence would move the AD 1000 figure.

title: The Chang'e-6 lunar cratering chronology
claim: The lunar cratering chronology function, revised with Chang'e-6 far-side samples (2.807 Ga basalts and 4.247 Ga South Pole–Aitken norite impact melts), shows near-side and far-side impact flux indistinguishable within uncertainty — a single unified global chronology in which impact activity declines smoothly and rapidly from planetary accretion, with no cataclysmic spike.

grade_reason: Two independent 2026 peer-reviewed studies (crater-count chronology and argon-isotope dating of far-side melts) converge on the same monotonic-decline curve; single-study lineage awaits further replication, so CORROBORATED, not higher.

sources.ref: Yue et al., Science Advances (2026), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.ady9265 — far-side-anchored lunar chronology: smooth rapid decline, no 3.9 Ga spike, unified global chronology
Zhang et al., Science Advances (23 July 2026) — independent argon-dating of 28 far-side impact melts confirms the monotonic decline
Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences research news (9 Feb 2026) — institutional summary

title: The moving substrate — the synthesis argument of master-list VIII.h
claim: The map's own ground moves: river avulsions, delta migrations, and shoreline shifts mean that ancient texts' geographic descriptions ("the port of X," "the mouth of the Y," "on the coast") cannot be pinned at their modern coordinates without a substrate baseline. Pins at excavated sites are stable (the site does not move); textual geography without a dated substrate reconstruction carries a precision grade no better than 'region' and risks tens-of-kilometers error. Demonstration exhibits: the Persian Gulf head (coastline at c. 5000 BCE near Eridu/Ur per Larsen & Evans 1978 / Lambeck 1996 / Sanlaville 1989, never reaching Uruk per Jotheri et al. 2018; Gulf reached its current configuration c. AD 1000 via Shatt al-Arab progradation), the Nile's defunct branches (Canopic branch — Naukratis's river — and Pelusiac branch silted; the Pelusiac's lower-reach death c. AD 25 per the 1973 Science survey; Pi-Ramesse/Qantir abandoned when its river dried), and the Yellow River's 1855 Tongwaxiang avulsion (Yellow Sea to Bohai).
place: Southern Mesopotamia / Nile Delta / North China Plain (three demonstration zones)
grade_reason: Each exhibit is independently attested by peer-reviewed geoarchaeology or survey: the Gulf-head reconstruction has multi-team convergence with the debate stated; the Pelusiac trace is a published Science survey; the 1855 avulsion is documented history. Chain strengthened 12→14 sources at the tenth pass (ep723): the 2026 Apollonia drowned-harbor study (tectonic ± sea-level, dated slipways) and the 2026 Northern Adriatic paleolandscape reconstruction (dated 8 m + 5 m rises, up to 25 mm/yr) join the shorelines-retreat arm as peer-reviewed exhibits.
earliest_attestation: Herodotus, Histories 2.17 — the seven mouths of the Nile (5th c. BCE), the oldest textual witness that a river's mouths are plural and movable.

sources.ref: Jotheri, Allen, et al. 2018 — Holocene fluvial and anthropogenic processes in the region of Uruk (marine transgression never reached the Uruk area, ~300 km from the present shoreline; discussion of the 6000 BP shoreline debate)

falsifiability: A dated, peer-reviewed substrate reconstruction showing that any one exhibit's ancient river-mouth or shoreline sat where the modern map puts it would retire that exhibit; the argument stands on the aggregate of independent reconstructions.

title: The White Temple on the Anu ziggurat, Uruk
claim: The Anu ziggurat at Uruk — the oldest known ziggurat, begun c. 4000 BCE and raised in at least ten rebuilds to ~12 m — carried the White Temple on its summit (Uruk III, c. 3500–3000 BCE): a 17.5 × 22.3 m tripartite temple, whitewashed inside and out, shining across the flat plain and visible over the city's walls.
place: Anu ziggurat, Uruk (Warka, Iraq)
grade_reason: Excavated, measured, and repeatedly rebuilt in visible stratigraphy — but the 'Anu' dedication is modern convention, and the labor figures are estimates; the record states both out loud.
earliest_attestation: The terrace and temple themselves (German Archaeological Institute excavations, Uruk, 1928–1939 and later)

sources.ref: German Archaeological Institute Uruk excavations — Anu district terrace (≥10 phases, ~12 m), White Temple summit building
phys.org synthesis (2026-01): the Anu ziggurat as the oldest known, White Temple 3500–3000 BCE, zaqāru etymology
Labor estimate: ~1,500 laborers × 10 hr/day × ~5 years for the last terrace revetment (modern calculation)
No-evidence caveat on the Anu dedication (modern literature's assumption, unattested)

competing_hypotheses: The 'Anu' dedication is assumed, not attested — there is no evidence Anu was worshipped in the structure; the temple's deity is unknown
The 1,500-laborer / 10-hour-day / 5-year construction estimate is a modern calculation, not an ancient record
Earlier terrace phases carried different superstructures — the White Temple is the last one, not the only one
falsifiability: Re-excavation showing the terrace is natural, or dating moving the phases millennia later

title: The Late Heavy Bombardment telling
claim: The inner solar system suffered a cataclysmic spike in impacts at ~3.9 billion years ago — the 'Late Heavy Bombardment' — a solar-system-wide storm of asteroids that scarred the Moon, Earth, and the terrestrial planets long after their formation.
place: Chang'e-6 landing site, Apollo crater, South Pole–Aitken Basin, lunar far side
grade_reason: Two independent 2026 peer-reviewed far-side studies (crater-chronology and argon-dating) find a smooth monotonic impact-flux decline with no 3.9 Ga spike; the original clustering was Imbrium-basin contamination of the near-side-only Apollo sample set.
earliest_attestation: Tera, Papanastassiou & Wasserburg, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 1974 — the 3.9 Ga clustering of Apollo impact-melt ages that built the hypothesis

sources.ref: Tera, Papanastassiou & Wasserburg, Earth and Planetary Science Letters 1974 — the original 3.9 Ga impact-melt age clustering from Apollo samples

Yue et al., Science Advances (2026), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.ady9265 — Chang'e-6 far-side samples: near- and far-side impact flux indistinguishable; smooth monotonic decline, no 3.9 Ga spike; 4.247 Ga SPA norites inconsistent with the LHB model and with sawtooth alternatives

Zhang et al., Science Advances (23 July 2026) — argon-isotope dating of 28 far-side impact melts from Chang'e-6: no clustering at 3.9 Ga; 'the lunar farside bombardment was not dominated by a cataclysmic spike' (Guangzhou Institute of Geochemistry)

Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences research news (9 Feb 2026) — institutional summary of the Yue et al. result: revised chronology, smooth decline, 'providing no support for the Late Heavy Bombardment hypothesis'

competing_hypotheses: A milder late dynamical-instability pulse (Nice-model late instability): a smaller, less synchronized flux bump — not ruled out by the 2026 work, but it is not the classic 3.9 Ga cataclysm
The sawtooth impact-flux scenario: explicitly inconsistent with the 4.247 Ga Chang'e-6 norite ages (Yue et al. 2026)
falsifiability: A statistically robust clustering of far-side impact-melt ages at ~3.9 Ga from an independent sample set, or a new far-side basin dated to ~3.9 Ga

title: Uruk, one of the world's first great cities
claim: Uruk in southern Mesopotamia grew into one of the world's first true cities, reaching urban scale (tens of thousands of inhabitants, monumental precincts like the Eanna) during the Uruk period, c. 3800-3200 BCE.
place: Uruk (Warka)
grade_reason: Extensive stratified archaeology shows urban-scale settlement and monumentality; the superlative 'first' is definitional, not evidential — and the northern evidence (Tell Brak) now names the definitional rival.
earliest_attestation: Archaeological strata (Uruk excavations, German Archaeological Institute, from 1912); contemporary tablets and cylinder seals

sources.ref: German Archaeological Institute Uruk excavations (stratigraphy, Eanna precinct)
Uruk-period tablets and administrative artifacts (CDLI corpus)
Pleiades gazetteer entry for Uruk
University of Cambridge Tell Brak survey (Ur, 2007): proto-urban center c. 4200-3900 BCE, concurrent with or earlier than Uruk

competing_hypotheses: Uruk is the first true city by population and monumentality criteria

Tell Brak (N Syria): proto-urban, walled, c. 4200-3900 BCE at 55 ha, with a 2006-07 Cambridge survey showing urban development concurrent with or earlier than Uruk — plus Khirbat al-Fakhar's ~300-ha low-density scatter (larger than contemporary Uruk) — making 'first' genuinely contested, not just definitional
Eridu or other centers qualify equally under looser definitions of urbanism
falsifiability: A securely dated, larger urban center predating Uruk's urban phase, or re-dating showing Uruk's urban phase is much later
