Gary Urton, 'Signs of the Inka Khipu' (2003): ~600 extant khipus estimated; the Open Khipu Repository holds 702 with public data (Jan 2026); a 2021 survey places known pre-Columbian khipus just under 1,400
Colonial chronicles describing quipucamayocs maintaining census, tribute, and storehouse records across Tawantinsuyu
Frank Salomon (1994, Tupicocha): khipus still used for local government record-keeping — a living tradition under observation

competing_hypotheses: Gary Urton's seven-bit binary-code hypothesis: khipus encode up to ~1,536 distinct signs via color, ply, attachment, knot type — far more than numbers need
The 'memory-aid only' view: some historians hold that only the individual quipucamayoc who made a khipu could read it, making it mnemonic rather than a true information system
falsifiability: Systematic failure of the decimal reading across newly excavated imperial-period khipus with clear archaeological context, or demonstration that knot placement is random/decorative rather than positional-numeric

title: The origin of Islam
claim: In 7th-century Arabia, the Qur'anic revelation proclaimed through Muhammad founded Islam; within a century of his death the caliphate stretched from Spain to Central Asia, and the Qur'anic text was standardized.
place: Mecca (traditional origin)
grade_reason: 7th-8th century manuscripts, monumental inscriptions, and independent external chronicles converge on Islam's 7th-century Arabian origin and rapid expansion.
earliest_attestation: Early Qur'anic manuscripts (Birmingham Mingana, Sanaa palimpsest — 7th-8th c.); the Dome of the Rock inscriptions (691 CE); non-Muslim chronicles of the conquests

Sanaa palimpsest (Dar al-Makhtutat, 7th-8th c.)
Dome of the Rock inscriptions (691 CE)
Sebeos, Armenian History (7th c. external account of the conquests)
PERF 558 (643 CE — bilingual Greek-Arabic receipt; the conquest era's own paperwork, documentary not traditional)

title: The Qur'anic attestation of the jinn
claim: The Qur'an attests jinn as created beings distinct from angels and humans: made of smokeless fire, created before Adam, addressed as moral agents (believers and unbelievers among them) alongside humans.
place: Mecca/Hijaz (traditional revelation setting)
grade_reason: The belief-phenomenon is multiply attested: the 7th-century text, its manuscript record, and the hadith layer all agree on fire-created, pre-Adamic, morally-agented jinn distinct from angels — graded as attestation, never as entities.
earliest_attestation: The Qur'anic text itself: Surah 72 (al-Jinn, 28 verses — a company of jinn hearing the Qur'an and converting, 72:1–14); Surah 55:15 (created from a smokeless flame of fire); Surah 15:26–27 (jinn created before Adam); Surah 51:56 (jinn and men created for service); Surah 18:50 (Iblis was 'of the jinn'); Surah 6:100, 6:128, 34:41 (the distinction from angels).

title: The 2026 Al-Ma'mala mosque: a first-century-Hijri mosque with a Muhammad-name qibla inscription

title: The Doctrina Iacobi (July 634 CE) — earliest non-Muslim writing on an Arabian prophet
claim: The Doctrina Iacobi nuper baptizati, a Byzantine Christian-Jewish polemic completed in Carthage before 13 July 634 CE, contains — in a letter from a certain Abraham in Caesarea — the earliest known non-Muslim writing to describe a prophet who 'has appeared among the Saracens': an armed figure proclaiming the advent of the anointed one and claiming the keys of paradise.
place: Carthage (composition); the prophet passage is set at Caesarea Maritima
grade_reason: Multiple manuscript copies preserve the passage; the internal indiction date is explicit and broadly accepted by scholars — but the passage names no name: it says only 'the prophet who has appeared with the Saracens.' The identification with Muhammad is the mainstream reading, not the text's own claim.
earliest_attestation: The tract itself — completed July 634 CE, i.e., about two years after Muhammad's traditional death date of 632 CE

sources.ref: Doctrina Iacobi nuper baptizati, V.16, 209 (ed. Bonwetsch; passage quoting the letter of Abraham in Caesarea)
Sean W. Anthony, 'Muhammad, the Keys to Paradise, and the Doctrina Iacobi: A Late Antique Puzzle' (Der Islam 91.2, 2014: 243-265)

competing_hypotheses: The passage is a contemporary reaction to the early conquests, preserving the earliest external echo of Muhammad's movement (mainstream reading)
The passage may describe a Jewish messianic claimant or a garbled secondhand report, not Muhammad himself (the cautious reading — the text never names him)
falsifiability: Manuscript evidence showing the prophet passage is a later interpolation, or a scholarly re-dating of the tract's composition decades after 634 CE

title: PERF 558 (643 CE) — the oldest dated Arabic document

place: Egypt (exact findspot unknown; held Vienna Papyrus Collection)
grade_reason: The document survives, is self-dated in both languages, and has been multiply published since 1894 — the Arabic text is 7th-century administration, not later recollection.
earliest_attestation: The papyrus itself, 643 CE — a primary bureaucratic document, a decade after the conquest of Egypt

sources.ref: PERF 558 (P.Vindob. inv. G 39726), Greek-Arabic tax protocol, 22 AH / 643 CE, issued under 'Abd Allah b. Jabr (primary, Vienna Papyrus Collection)
J. von Karabacek, Papyrus Erzherzog Rainer Führer (PERF), 1894 — the editio princeps

sources.ref: The Zuhayr graffito, self-dated 24 AH, al-Ula region (primary)
The Arabic epigraphic literature on early Islamic graffiti (the graffito is the field's standard earliest securely dated Islamic-era example)

title: Pakal's sarcophagus lid ('Palenque astronaut')
claim: The sarcophagus lid of K'inich Janaab' Pakal the Great (603–683 CE) depicts him piloting a spacecraft (the 'Palenque astronaut').
place: Temple of the Inscriptions, Palenque, Chiapas, Mexico
grade_reason: Every element the spaceship reading calls machinery maps to known Maya cosmology: the 'exhaust flames' are the open jaws of the jaguar/Xibalba below, the 'capsule' is Pakal reclining in death, the 'antenna' is the cosmic tree (Wacah Chan) rising behind him to the celestial bird (Itzam-Ye). The surrounding inscriptions read as ancestral record, per Palenque dynastic epigraphy.
earliest_attestation: The lid itself, discovered in situ by Alberto Ruz Lhuillier in 1952 in the Temple of the Inscriptions, Palenque

sources.ref: Temple of the Inscriptions — sarcophagus lid description: Pakal between the heavens and the underworld, cosmic tree, serpent bar, ancestors in six-generation line
ThoughtCo: the lid depicts Pakal 'being reborn into eternal life... along with the cosmic tree' emerging from the earth monster with the quadripartite sun monster

competing_hypotheses: The lid depicts Pakal's fall into Xibalba (the Maya underworld) and ascent via the World Tree (Wacah Chan) — rebirth iconography, the scholarly reading
The spaceship reading relies on rotating the image 90° out of its intended orientation and ignoring the surrounding cosmology

The glyphic record says otherwise: the lid's edge inscriptions list prior rulers — a dynastic death list, not a flight manual.

title: The Dome of the Rock inscriptions (72 AH / 691–92 CE)
claim: The Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, dedicated 72 AH / 691–92 CE, carries about 240 meters of Arabic inscription — including Qur'anic verses and paraphrases — making it the oldest securely dated Qur'anic text in the world: the date belongs to the writing itself, not to the material it is written on.

Estelle Whelan, 'Inscriptions in the Dome of the Rock and their reinterpretation' — the anti-Trinitarian polemic reading (Q 4:171, 19:33–35, 112) and the verse-selection argument
Oleg Grabar, The Dome of the Rock — the monument's Umayyad context and inscription program

The inscription program was aimed inward, at sectarian Muslim audiences (Whelan's reinterpretation emphasis)
