The de-jure/de-facto distinction: some historians argue the 1920 date is still the right landmark because the barriers that survived were racial, not sexual. The record's reply: the popular claim being graded is about WOMEN, and the women excluded were women — the asterisk is sex-plus-race, and the grade covers the claim as stated.
falsifiability: Proof that Native American, Chinese American, and Southern Black women voted freely and unobstructed in the 1920 elections would collapse the record. The opposite is what the sources show.

title: The Coso artifact (500,000-year-old spark plug claim)
claim: The Coso artifact — a device found inside a 500,000-year-old geode at Olancha, California, in 1961 — is an ancient or advanced-technology object (Atlantis, ancient astronauts, time travelers).
place: Olancha, California (reported find site)
grade_reason: X-ray investigation plus the 2018 physical inspection identify the device as a 1920s-era Champion spark plug; the 'geode' is a rust concretion that forms in decades; the 500,000-year figure was never published by anyone.
earliest_attestation: February 1961 collection by Mike Mikesell, Virginia Hahn and Wallace Lane at Olancha, California; the '500,000-year' figure comes from an unnamed, unpublished geologist's letter

sources.ref: Stromberg & Heinrich x-ray investigation with the Spark Plug Collectors of America (Chad Windham, Bill Bond, Mike Healy, Jeff Bartheld): the object is a 1920s-era Champion spark plug, the type used in Ford Model T and Model A engines; the 'brass hat' explains the rib

12 April 2018 physical inspection (Stromberg + University of Washington geologist): confirmed the spark-plug identification; no fossil shells found — undercutting the shell-dating claim the fame rested on
The stone matrix is an iron-oxide concretion from the rusting plug — such concretions form over decades or years, not millennia (Cronyn)
Pacific Science Center, Seattle — the artifact displayed in the 'What Is Reality?' exhibition (as of 2019)

competing_hypotheses: The pseudoscientific readings (ancient advanced civilization, ancient astronauts, human time travelers) — documented in the literature as hypotheses, killed by the object itself
Deliberate fraud by the 1961 discoverers — Heinrich & Stromberg found 'little hard evidence' the discoverers intended to deceive anyone
falsifiability: A documented in-situ excavation with geological dating of the matrix — or material evidence inconsistent with a 1920s Champion spark plug

title: The Great Wall visible from the Moon / from space with the naked eye
claim: The Great Wall of China is visible with the naked eye from the Moon — and/or is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye.
place: The claim is about the Wall seen from afar; pin carried as Badaling representative section
grade_reason: Direct eyewitness testimony from Moon-walkers and orbiters falsifies the naked-eye claim, and optical physics makes it impossible: the human eye resolves ~1 arcminute; a 6-m-wide wall at lunar distance subtends ~1/10,000 of an arcminute — 'seeing a human hair from a kilometer away'.
earliest_attestation: Ripley's Believe It or Not cartoon, 1932: 'the mightiest work of man, the only one that would be visible to the human eye from the moon'; an earlier form appears in William Henry Hudson's 'Dead Man's Plack and an Old Thorn' (1920)

sources.ref: Ripley's Believe It or Not cartoon, 1932 (origin of the popular Moon-visibility form)
Neil Armstrong: 'definitely not visible from the Moon'; Michael Collins, Liftoff (1988); Jim Lovell ('the claim is absurd'); Jim Irwin ('out of the question') — primary astronaut testimony
Jay Apt, National Geographic, Nov 1996: 'made largely of materials that have the same color as the surrounding soil ... almost invisible from only 180 miles up'
Yang Liwei (Shenzhou 5, 2003): 'I didn't see the Great Wall' — CCTV interview; China's Ministry of Education subsequently revised textbooks
Dai Changda, Jiang Xiaoguang, Xi Xiaohuan (CAS), Science and Technology Review, 2007: a 10-m-wide object is naked-eye visible from at most 36 km in ideal weather — below the 100 km space boundary
Scientific American (Phil Plait): from ISS altitude the wall subtends ~0.1 arcminute (eye limit ~1 arcminute); from the Moon, 1/10,000 arcminute

competing_hypotheses: Gene Cernan (Apollo 17, 2004): 'in Earth's orbit at a height of 160 to 320 km, the Great Wall of China is indeed visible to the naked eye' — the minority astronaut dissent, named fairly

Telephoto/high-resolution orbital imagery can capture wall sections under ideal conditions (e.g. ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst, ISS, 2018, 800mm lens); radar imagery (SIR aboard Shuttle Endeavour) shows it readily — the honest replacements: cameras see what eyes cannot
falsifiability: A controlled naked-eye sighting from lunar distance with confirmed identification (extraordinary, given the optics); from low orbit, a confirmed identification under documented conditions would only soften the low-orbit leg

title: 'KDKA made the first radio broadcast' (2 Nov 1920) — DEBUNKED
claim: Pittsburgh's KDKA made the first radio broadcast in history on 2 November 1920, when it transmitted the Harding-Cox presidential election returns.
place: East Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania (Westinghouse plant shack)
grade_reason: The 'first broadcast' is a textbook shorthand killed by the pre-1920 record: Frank Conrad's own 8XK was making semi-regular entertainment broadcasts from October 1919; 8MK Detroit was on the air August 1920; XWA Montreal late 1919; Radio Argentina August 1920; Charles Herrold's San Jose station was airing regular programs for a general audience by 1912 (on the air 1909); Lee de Forest broadcast music from the Eiffel Tower in 1908. Even the 'first commercial license' reading fails: the first U.S. commercial license went to WBZ (Sept 1921), not KDKA. KDKA's genuine achievement — the first license issued for the specific purpose of broadcasting, and the election-night program that riveted national attention — is fenced out of the kill.
earliest_attestation: Contemporary 1920 sources: the Pittsburgh Post's own coverage of the election-night program; IEEE milestone text quotes the broadcast's own words ('Will anyone hearing this broadcast please communicate with us...'); the station's first official listing in the July 1, 1916 Radio Stations of the United States as amateur experimental 8XK (the antecedent)

sources.ref: IEEE Engineering and Technology History Wiki, 'Milestones: Westinghouse Radio Station KDKA, 1920' — 2 Nov 1920 election-night broadcast, 18 hours, the antecedent 8XK (1916); the milestone text documents the event it celebrates

Wikipedia, 'KQV' — 8MK Detroit on air Aug 1920; KDKA's 1946 'world's first regularly scheduled broadcast' claim and the pre-dating challengers (KQV, WWJ, KCBS); Conrad's 8XK semi-regular broadcasts from 17 Oct 1919

title: The 1921 Nobel Prize (photoelectric effect, not relativity)

title: Farnsworth's first all-electronic TV transmission (7 Sept 1927)
claim: On 7 September 1927, at his laboratory at 202 Green Street, San Francisco, 21-year-old Philo Farnsworth transmitted the first all-electronic television image: his image-dissector camera aimed at a glass slide with a single painted line, the line appearing live on a cathode-ray-tube receiver in the next room — and rotating when the slide was rotated.
place: 202 Green Street, San Francisco, California
grade_reason: The 1927 transmission is attested by the lab party and corroborated by independent lines: the January 1927 patent filing (US 1,773,980) predates the demo, the 3 September 1928 press demonstration was witnessed by independent reporters (first image: a dollar sign), the 25 August 1934 Franklin Institute public demo, and Tolman's preserved 1922 sketch that carried the 1935 interference ruling. Held below VERIFIED because the September 1927 moment itself rests on the inventor's own party — the independent witnesses arrive in 1928.
earliest_attestation: Farnsworth laboratory record and the lab party's account, 7 September 1927; patent application for the television system filed 7 January 1927 (US 1,773,980); contemporary press coverage of the 3 September 1928 demonstration

sources.ref: Wikipedia, 'Philo Farnsworth': 'demonstrated the first working version on September 7, 1927, having turned 21 the previous August'; first demonstrated to the press 3 September 1928; public demo at the Franklin Institute, 25 August 1934; image dissector converted image elements into electricity one at a time

The Philo T. Farnsworth Archives / weeklyview.net: 202 Green Street lab; the glass slide backlit by an arc lamp; the 1928 press demo's first image (a dollar sign); 1929 first live human images (wife Pem, eyes closed against the light)
US Patent 1,773,980 (filed 7 January 1927) — the television-system patent whose Claim 15 ('electrical image') became the count in Interference No. 64,027

competing_hypotheses: The press-demo reading: the 7 September date rests on the lab party's own record; the first *independently witnessed* transmission is the 3 September 1928 press demonstration (and the 25 August 1934 Franklin Institute public demo) — a strict evidentiary bar would date the public record to 1928, not 1927.

The mechanical-priority reading: John Logie Baird's 1926 public demonstration of a working television system predates Farnsworth's — if 'television' is not restricted to the electronic method, the first transmission belongs to the mechanical line; the electronic qualifier is doing the work.

The Zworykin-co-invention reading: Zworykin's 1923 Westinghouse patent application predates Farnsworth's 1927 filing, and Zworykin built on the same electron-scanning logic — the interference settled *priority on Claim 15*, not sole inventorship of the whole field.

The date-precision reading: Farnsworth worked out the image-dissector principle in summer 1921 and the device evolved through 1927; fixing 'television invented' to a single September day is a historiographic convenience — the achievement is a span, not a point.
falsifiability: A contemporary (1927) independent record contradicting the transmission — or period evidence that the 1927 apparatus could not have worked as described — would move the grade down; a 1927 notebook entry from a party independent of Farnsworth's lab witnessing the transmission would move it up.
