evt-pray-codex-shroud-illumination-001 (the CORROBORATED illumination the telling overclaims from)

competing_hypotheses: The identification is correct and the codex is a genuine pre-1355 witness to the Turin Shroud (unfalsified — graded CLAIMED, never DEBUNKED; see evt-pray-codex-shroud-illumination-001)
falsifiability: Already falsified as a proof-claim: proof requires ruling out the conventional-iconography alternative, which no study has done. The telling dies; the identification question stays open.

title: Assmann's counterhistory: the Exodus as deliberate inversion
claim: Jan Assmann's thesis that the biblical Exodus narrative functions as a 'counterhistory' — a deliberate literary inversion of the Egyptian account preserved by Manetho (via Josephus): expulsion becomes liberation, the expelled become the chosen, the kings become the slaves, the lepers/polluted become the elect. Assmann developed this in Moses the Egyptian (Harvard UP, 1997) and later works; mnemohistory studies the remembered past, not the past as such.
place: Heidelberg (Assmann's university; the thesis, not the events)
grade_reason: A reasoned scholarly interpretation of a literary relationship; the deliberate intentionality (composed AS an inversion) is unattested in any ancient source — no text tells us the Exodus authors knew Manetho's account or wrote against it.
earliest_attestation: Jan Assmann, Moses the Egyptian: The Memory of Egypt in Western Monotheism (Harvard UP, 1997); elaborated in The Invention of Religion (2018)

sources.ref: Jan Assmann, Moses the Egyptian (Harvard UP, 1997) — mnemohistory, the 'Mosaic distinction', counter-religion cycle
Josephus, Contra Apion 1.26-31 (the Manetho quotation the thesis inverts against)
Wikipedia, 'Moses the Egyptian' — summary: book described as mnemohistory; wide acclaim, heavily discussed among Egyptologists and religious-studies scholars
Chronicle of Higher Education, 'Biblical Blame Shift' — Assmann's 'Mosaic distinction' and the international controversy over The Price of Monotheism

tis.so, 'The Principle of Normative Inversion,' mid-Sept 2026 — popular/theoretical essay extending Assmann's inversion lens (Tacitus on the Jews, Manetho, Maimonides' Sabians as 'inversion-of-inversions'); theoretical engagement, not new Assmann scholarship and not evidence about the Exodus authors' intentions

competing_hypotheses: The Osarseph story is the Egyptian/Hellenistic side's inversion OF the Exodus narrative (direction reversed: Exodus first, anti-Jewish counter-narrative second)
No literary relationship at all — both stories draw independently on shared folk memories (Amarna, Hyksos expulsions)
Assmann's own composite reading: the Osarseph story combines multiple historical experiences, so there is no single text being inverted
The Exodus narrative encodes the Hyksos expulsion (c. 1550 BCE) without any counterhistory mechanism
falsifiability: An ancient text stating the Exodus authors' literary sources or intentions; or a securely dated pre-Manetho Egyptian text containing the leper-expulsion plot, which would collapse the direction-of-inversion question

title: Deep Blue defeats Kasparov, 1997
claim: The 1997 Deep Blue–Kasparov rematch (3–11 May 1997, Equitable Center, New York City) ended 3½–2½ to IBM's Deep Blue — the first defeat of a reigning world chess champion by a computer under standard tournament time controls.
place: Equitable Center, New York City
grade_reason: Multiple independent primary/contemporary sources converge: the published game scores (Kasparov win G1, Deep Blue wins G2/G6, draws G3/G4/G5), the IBM team records, and contemporaneous worldwide reporting of Game 6's 19-move resignation.
earliest_attestation: Contemporary match records, game scores, and worldwide press coverage, May 1997

sources.ref: Murray Campbell, A. Joseph Hoane Jr., Feng-hsiung Hsu, 'Deep Blue', Artificial Intelligence 134(1–2), 57–83 (2002) — the builders' own technical account: 32-node IBM RS/6000 SP, 256 dedicated VLSI chess processors, ~100–200 million positions/second

Contemporary match reportage: Kasparov won Game 1, Deep Blue Game 2 (the first computer win over a world champion under tournament controls), draws in Games 3–5, Deep Blue's Game 6 win; Kasparov's post-match 'human intervention' remarks reported in press
The Harvard Crimson, 12 May 1997 — contemporary commentary establishing the match's documented character ('didn't and couldn't learn a single thing throughout the match')

competing_hypotheses: Kasparov's 1997 'human intervention' allegation — attested (he said the Game 2 play felt human) but never evidenced; graded separately, never the event
The 'it was only a chess match' reading — true as scope, false as dismissal: the match's significance was the demonstrated engineering milestone, not chess itself
falsifiability: Contemporary game scores or tournament records contradicting the 3½–2½ result, or evidence the match was not played under standard controls

title: The 'Deep Blue thought like a human' myth
claim: Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov in 1997 by out-thinking him — playing and thinking like a human chess player, demonstrating machine intelligence in the human sense.
place: Equitable Center, New York City (the match's site)
grade_reason: Disproven by the builders' own published technical account (Campbell, Hoane & Hsu 2002): Deep Blue was a 32-node RS/6000 SP with 256 dedicated VLSI chess processors searching ~100–200 million positions per second with hand-crafted evaluation, a grandmaster-built opening library (GM Joel Benjamin), and endgame tablebases — no learning capability in the match build. The 'thinking' was a brute-force search tree with human-written chess knowledge; the machine could not learn a single thing during the match (contemporary Crimson commentary, 12 May 1997). The victory is real; the reading of it as machine 'thought' is not.
earliest_attestation: 1997 worldwide press and IBM marketing framing of the match as an 'intelligent machine' victory; Kasparov's own post-match claim that the play felt human

sources.ref: Campbell, Hoane & Hsu, 'Deep Blue', Artificial Intelligence 134(1–2), 57–83 (2002) — 200M positions/sec, alpha-beta search, hand-tuned evaluation, grandmaster opening book; no in-match learning

The Harvard Crimson, 12 May 1997 — 'Deep Blue didn't and couldn't learn a single thing throughout the match, as it relied on its sheer processing power to calculate its next move. Relentless computation is not artificial intelligence.' (contemporary counterweight to the hype framing)
Kasparov's post-match remarks (1997) — the 'human-aid' suspicion reported in press; allegation attested, evidence never produced (kept as competing hypothesis, not as the debunk's target)

competing_hypotheses: The honest-engineering reading: Deep Blue's victory demonstrated brute-force computation plus human engineering — a genuine milestone, just not a thinking one (the fence the debunk protects)
Kasparov's 'human intervention' allegation (1997): attested but never evidenced — IBM's logs were never shown to disprove it to his satisfaction, but no evidence for it has ever surfaced either
falsifiability: IBM's match-build logs showing self-modifying strategy or in-match learning — the builders' published account says the opposite

title: The pine cone as hygrometer (verified folk instrument)
claim: Pine cones open their scales when good (dry) weather is coming and close them when wet weather approaches — the cone is a working hygrometer.
place: Freiburg, Germany (livMatS biomechanics research; folk use universal in temperate pine regions)
grade_reason: The mechanism is published and replicated: each scale is a functional bilayer — a highly swellable lower sclereid layer and a far less swellable upper layer — that acts like a bimetallic strip responding to humidity instead of heat (Nature Scientific Reports). Under wet conditions the scales curve up and the cone closes, protecting the wind-dispersed seeds; under dry conditions they bend down and release them. The Freiburg livMatS team (2022, Advanced Science) analyzed the tissue structures in detail; the motion is passive, deterministic, and already used as a model for biomimetic moisture-reactive building systems (Stuttgart's HygroScope, Urbach Tower). The folk reading — open = dry/fair, closed = wet — tracks the physics.
earliest_attestation: Antique folk use of pine cones (and seaweed) as humidity indicators; the mechanism literature from Dawson et al. 1997

sources.ref: Nature Scientific Reports, 'Hygroscopic motions of fossil conifer cones': 'The opening and closing of woody conifer cones... is governed by a hygroscopic swelling/shrinking mechanism... Under wet conditions... the pine scales are curved upwards, the cone is closed and the winged, airborne seeds are protected... Under dry conditions, however, the scales bend down and liberate the seeds.' The scale as 'a functional bilayer' reacting 'similarly to a bimetallic strip, but responds to humidity changes instead of heat.'

Phys.org / University of Freiburg livMatS (2022, Advanced Science): 'Pine cones open when dry and close when wet. In this way, pine seeds are released only under advantageous conditions, namely when it is dry and the seeds can be carried far by wind.' The actuation 'does not consume metabolic energy' — passive, deterministic; already a model for biomimetic building envelopes.

Museum of the Earth / Earth@Home (4-H curriculum): 'Pinecones are Mother Nature's hygrometers... pinecones only open their scales to disperse the seeds when the air is dry, and they close their scales when the air is moist to protect the seeds and keep them dry.'

Dairy Diary (UK), '7 Weather Folklore Sayings': 'Pine cones open up when good weather is coming. This is one of the few sayings that is based on scientific fact. In dry weather, pine cones dry out, which causes their scales to stand out with a more "open" appearance. In wet weather, the scales curl up and the cones return to a more closed shape.'

competing_hypotheses: The cone as a future-predictor (fenced: the cone measures current humidity, not the future — but humidity trends precede weather changes, and the folk reading tracks the mechanism faithfully enough to stand)
The cone as pure coincidence (refuted by the biomechanics: the motion is a deterministic hygroscopic response, published and replicated)
falsifiability: A controlled humidity-chamber study showing pine-cone scales do not move deterministically with humidity — the opposite of every published result

title: The Toba bottleneck hypothesis (1998) — the causality question
claim: The volcanic-winter bottleneck hypothesis (Ambrose 1998, Journal of Human Evolution): the Youngest Toba Tuff (~74 ka) triggered years of global cooling — a volcanic winter — that collapsed the human population to a few thousand breeding individuals, creating the genetic bottleneck read in the mitochondrial and Y-chromosome coalescences.
place: Lake Toba (the cause); the claimed effect is global
grade_reason: A reasoned, peer-reviewed hypothesis with a real eruption behind it — but the causal chain is contested on the archaeology (Jwalapuram continuity), the ecology (Malawi stability), and the genetics (coalescences mostly pre-date the ash). Unattested as a causal claim; grade stays SPECULATION.
earliest_attestation: Ambrose 1998, Journal of Human Evolution: 'Late Pleistocene human population bottlenecks, volcanic winter, and differentiation of modern humans'

sources.ref: Ambrose 1998, Journal of Human Evolution — the original volcanic-winter bottleneck hypothesis
Williams et al. 2009 — GISP2 ice-core sulfate at ~74 ka, the quantitative anchor for the volcanic-winter loading
Petraglia et al. 2007, Science — Jwalapuram locality C: Middle Paleolithic industries above and below the Toba ash — the continuity rebuttal
Lane et al. 2013 — Lake Malawi cores: no local ecological collapse at ~74 ka
Gathorne-Hardy & Harcourt-Smith 2003 — the refutation of a global near-extinction reading
The mtDNA/Y-chromosome coalescence windows (see the Coalescent bench, #384) — mostly older than the ash

competing_hypotheses: The Jwalapuram rebuttal: Petraglia et al. 2007, Science — Middle Paleolithic tool industries at Jwalapuram locality C (India) occur directly ABOVE and below the Toba ash: the people in India lived through the ash and kept making the same tools (Petraglia et al. 2012 review)
The Malawi record: Lane et al. 2013 — Lake Malawi cores show the lake did not dry and local vegetation did not collapse at ~74 ka; no local ecological crash in the African record where it was sought

The clock problem: mitochondrial Eve (99–200 ka) and Y-chromosomal Adam (~200–300 ka) coalescences mostly PRE-DATE Toba — the squeeze the clocks measure is older than the ash (Donal Friel's Coalescent bench)

The effective-vs-census distinction: 'a few thousand effective' is not 'a few thousand people' — effective population size is a genetic quantity, and census populations are larger; the popular telling routinely drops this distinction
The Gathorne-Hardy & Harcourt-Smith 2003 alternative: volcanic winters kill unevenly — local refugia, behavioral flexibility, and the Southern Coast record make a global near-extinction an over-read
falsifiability: No single agreed falsifier — the hypothesis's supporters and critics read different archives. It would be decisively weakened by a dated demographic record (not a clock inference) showing population continuity across the ash in multiple regions; it would be decisively strengthened by a dated, quantified, globally coherent crash timed exactly to the isochron. Grade stays SPECULATION either way until that exists.

title: The 1998 Lancet MMR-autism fraud (DEBUNKED)
claim: MMR vaccination causes autism (the claim built on Wakefield et al.'s 1998 Lancet paper).
place: Royal Free Hospital, Hampstead, London (Wakefield's 1998 research base)
grade_reason: Four independent kills: (1) Deer's 2004 Sunday Times investigation exposed undisclosed payment from the anti-MMR lawsuit's lawyers plus Wakefield's patent on a rival single-measles vaccine; (2) 10 of 12 co-authors retracted the interpretation (March 2004); (3) the GMC (January 2010) found dishonest research and unnecessary invasive procedures on developmentally delayed children without ethical approval — struck off May 2010; (4) The Lancet fully retracted (February 2010, 'utterly false'); the BMJ called it 'an elaborate fraud' (January 2011). The claim itself fails on epidemiology: Madsen 2002 (537,303 children) and Hviid 2019 (657,461; adjusted HR 0.93) find no association.
earliest_attestation: Wakefield et al., 'Ileal-lymphoid-nodular hyperplasia, non-specific colitis, and pervasive developmental disorder in children', The Lancet 351(9103):637-641, 28 February 1998 (fully retracted 2010).

sources.ref: Wakefield et al. 1998, The Lancet 351(9103):637-641 — the paper; fully retracted February 2010, editor-in-chief Richard Horton: 'utterly false', journal 'deceived'

Deer, B. — Sunday Times investigation 2004: undisclosed payment from the Legal Aid Board lawyers pursuing the anti-MMR lawsuit; Wakefield held a patent on a rival single-measles vaccine; 10 of 12 co-authors retracted the interpretation (March 2004)

General Medical Council verdict 28 January 2010: dishonest research; acted against patients' best interests; developmentally delayed children subjected to unnecessary invasive procedures (colonoscopy, lumbar puncture) without ethical approval; struck off the Medical Register 24 May 2010
BMJ, January 2011: Godlee editorial — 'an elaborate fraud'; Deer's BMJ series showing the medical records were falsified (children did not have the inflammatory bowel disease the paper reported)
Madsen et al. 2002, NEJM — 537,303 Danish children: no association between MMR and autism

Hviid et al. 2019, Annals of Internal Medicine — 'Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccination and Autism: A Nationwide Cohort Study': 657,461 Danish children (born 1999-2010), fully adjusted hazard ratio 0.93 — no increased risk, including in susceptible subgroups (siblings with autism); follow-up to the 2002 study
Cochrane systematic review 2020 — no evidence of increased autism risk from MMR/MMRV

competing_hypotheses: The 'too many too soon' / temporal-association concern — the honest parental observation of timing (autism diagnosis age overlaps the MMR schedule) that the fraud exploited; the timing is real, the causation is not

The thimerosal-mercury branch — a separate claim from the MMR one; thimerosal was removed from US childhood vaccines by 2001 as a precaution, and autism rates did not fall — fenced as a different record
falsifiability: A replicated, independently reproduced study with raw-data access showing elevated autism risk after MMR; instead, two decades of population studies (Denmark 537k + 657k, UK, US, Taylor 2014 meta-analysis, Cochrane 2020) show no association.

title: The 2001 NORC Media Recount of Florida 2000
claim: The 2001 NORC media recount of Florida's 2000 presidential ballots showed George W. Bush would have kept Florida under every recount strategy Al Gore actually pursued — and that Al Gore could only have won under a full statewide recount of all uncounted ballots (undervotes plus overvotes) that was never requested and never happened.
place: Florida, USA (statewide; 67 counties)
grade_reason: The study's findings are multiply and independently reported by the sponsoring news organizations themselves (AP, NYT, WaPo, FactCheck.org) on the same NORC-coded dataset: 175,010 rejected ballots examined ballot-by-ballot over ten months — the most thorough re-examination of the election ever conducted.
earliest_attestation: The consortium's release, 11 Nov 2001 (AP, New York Times, Washington Post, et al.); the NORC-coded ballot database of 175,010 rejected ballots across all 67 Florida counties.

sources.ref: Wikipedia, '2000 United States presidential election recount in Florida' — NORC outcomes table: Gore's four-county strategy Bush by 225; FL Supreme Court order Bush by 430; FL Supreme Court order as implemented Bush by 493; full statewide review with uniform standard Gore by 60–171; the media consortium's conclusion quoted

FactCheck.org, 'The Florida Recount of 2000' — the NORC study: 175,010 ballots examined by trained investigators; AP: 'George W. Bush would have narrowly prevailed in the partial recounts sought by Al Gore, but Gore might have reversed the outcome — by the barest of margins — had he pursued and gained a complete statewide recount'; sponsors listed (AP, NYT, WSJ, CNN, St. Petersburg Times, Palm Beach Post, Washington Post, Tribune Co.)

USA Today / earlier media consortium (May 2001) via the same article: 'George W. Bush would have won a hand recount of all disputed ballots... if the most widely accepted standard for judging votes had been applied'; a Gore win was impossible without a recount of overvotes, which he did not request

The NORC study's own caveat: 'But no study of this type can accurately recreate Election Day 2000 or predict what might have emerged from individual battles over more than 6 million votes in Florida's 67 counties.'

competing_hypotheses: The deHaven-Smith / Freeman & Bleifuss reading: under the most reasonable interpretations of the Florida Supreme Court's order — including overvotes, which Judge Terry Lewis was likely to order had the recount proceeded — Gore would have won even within the court-ordered framework. Named and held; it disputes which scenario counts as 'Gore's strategy,' not the NORC numbers themselves.

The legal-finality position: the certified result (Bush +537) is the only operative outcome; the NORC scenarios are hypotheticals that cannot recreate the county-by-county legal battles of Election Day. The NORC study itself carries this caveat.
falsifiability: A full ballot-level re-examination of the 175,010 rejected ballots producing materially different scenario margins, or a demonstrated coding-protocol flaw in NORC's review — neither has appeared in 25 years.

title: The Interstate 'one mile in five' landing-strip rule (DEBUNKED)
claim: The United States Interstate Highway System was designed so that one mile in every five is straight, for use as emergency landing strips for airplanes in wartime.
place: United States (the Interstate Highway System)
grade_reason: The Federal Highway Administration's own 'Interstate Highway System — The Myths' page kills the reading outright — the claim has no basis in law, regulation, design manual, or fact — and the documented root (the 1941 Act's Section 108 flight strips, placed near highways) explains the confusion without saving the claim.
earliest_attestation: Richard F. Weingroff's May/June 2000 Public Roads article 'Interstates as Runways: It 'Aint So' — responding to a claim already widespread on the Internet and in reference sources.

sources.ref: FHWA, 'Interstate Highway System — The Myths' — 'One in five miles of the Interstate System is straight so airplanes can land in emergencies': 'This myth is widespread on the Internet and in reference sources, but has no basis in law, regulation, design manual—or fact. Airplanes occasionally land on Interstates when no alternative is available in an emergency, not because the Interstates are designed for that purpose.'

Richard F. Weingroff, 'Interstates as Runways: It 'Aint So' (Public Roads, May/June 2000) — the FHWA information liaison specialist traces the myth's root to the Defense Highway Act of 1941, Section 108's flight-strip program (PRA + Army Air Force strips near highways); notes the 1944 Act came close to including another flight-strip program but did not, and the 1956 Act contains no such language

HowStuffWorks, 'Were U.S. Interstates Really Designed as Runways?' — the Defense Highway Act provided flight strips mostly for military use that were near highways; all three acts (1941, 1944, 1956) are real, none contains the one-in-five language
Lead Stories fact check, 2021-06 — the recirculating Facebook 'Fun fact of the day' post ('The Eisenhower interstate system requires that one mile in every five must be straight...') rated not true

competing_hypotheses: The myth is a misquotation of the Defense Highway Act of 1941's Section 108 flight-strip program, which put strips NEAR highways — the documented historical root (Weingroff 2000)
The reading has a German echo: some autobahn sections were used as auxiliary airstrips in WWII and the Cold War — carried as an unattested alternative root, not documented in the consulted sources
falsifiability: Produce the law, regulation, or design manual containing the one-mile-in-five requirement — the FHWA's challenge; none has ever been produced because no such text exists.

title: The category rehabilitated: dying-and-rising gods before Christianity
claim: The category 'dying-and-rising gods' names a real, pre-Christian phenomenon of attested death-and-return narratives in the ancient Near East — Osiris, Dumuzi/Tammuz, Baal, Melqart attested; Adonis and Eshmun probable — rehabilitated by Mettinger (2001) against the 1990s consensus ('they died but did not return'), which overstated its case. The category is a scholarly instrument graded on the columns, and the claim that early Christianity borrowed a ready-made 'resurrection template' from it remains unattested transmission — CLAIMED, not evidence.
place: Lund, Sweden (Mettinger's chair; historiographical anchor — the map pins the argument, not a place)
grade_reason: The rehabilitation is demonstrated per column in this pass (evt-osiris-dying-rising-001, evt-dumuzi-dying-rising-001, evt-baal-return-001 CORROBORATED as belief-phenomena; evt-attis-dying-rising-001 CLAIMED as the weakest). The 1990s consensus overstated; Mettinger's case-by-case perusal stands. The borrowing thesis is fenced separately.
earliest_attestation: Frazer, The Golden Bough (1890–1915) — the category's invention; J.Z. Smith, 'Dying and Rising Gods' (in Eliade's Encyclopedia of Religion, 1987) — the 'Drudgery Divine' dismissal; Mettinger, The Riddle of Resurrection (2001) — the rehabilitation

sources.ref: Mettinger, Tryggve N.D., The Riddle of Resurrection: 'Dying and Rising Gods' in the Ancient Near East (Coniectanea Biblica OT Series; Eisenbrauns, 2001) — 'The category of dying and rising gods is not a phantom construct'; five defended cases
Frazer, J.G., The Golden Bough (1890–1915) — the category's Victorian invention
Smith, Jonathan Z., 'Dying and Rising Gods' (Encyclopedia of Religion, 1987) — the 'Drudgery Divine' dismissal and the 1990s consensus
This pass's five columns: evt-osiris-dying-rising-001, evt-dumuzi-dying-rising-001, evt-baal-return-001, evt-adonis-dying-rising-001, evt-attis-dying-rising-001

BMCR 2002.09.07 — review of Mettinger, The Riddle of Resurrection: 'Dying and Rising Gods' in the Ancient Near East (Almqvist & Wiksell, 2001) — the reviewer's conclusion restates the held dispute: the category is 'a rather simplistic generalization for a very wide array of gods and a very murky range of rituals'; Osiris stands apart as a 'dead' god, not a dying-and-rising one; Greek Adonis lacks the resurrection stage; Dumuzi-Tammuz's 'rising' is embedded in ritual procession, not asserted as myth

competing_hypotheses: The 1990s consensus (J.Z. Smith 'Drudgery Divine' and others): the category is a Frazerian Victorian construct — 'dying and rising gods' died but did not return; the parallels are manufactured by selective comparison
The borrowing thesis: early Christianity drew its resurrection narrative from the pagan template — reasoned, unattested as transmission; no first-century Christian text cites the pagan columns
Mettinger's own fence: the pattern 'does not require uniformity' — Baal, Dumuzi, Melqart, Osiris differ in kind, and the category is an analytic tool, not a discovered natural kind
The maximalist reading: the category proves metaphysical truth about resurrection — not graded; the attestation rule grades beliefs, never entities
falsifiability: A demonstration that all five defended columns are post-Christian, or that Mettinger's textual readings are all wrong, would collapse the rehabilitation

title: 'Like painting the Forth Bridge' — the never-ending job (DEBUNKED)
claim: Painting the Forth Bridge is a never-ending task — a job that must begin again the moment it is finished, because by the time one end is painted the other end already needs a fresh coat.
place: Firth of Forth, Scotland
grade_reason: Two independent kills: (1) the event — the 2002–2011 restoration ended the continuous cycle: old paint blasted to bare metal, triple layer of specialist glass-flake epoxy (offshore-oil-industry chemistry, W J Leigh), designed to last 25 years; on 9 December 2011 the bridge was scaffolding-free for the first time in a decade and 'no additional full-scale repainting will be needed for at least 20 years'; (2) the owner's own words — Network Rail's Iain Coucher: the restoration would 'preserve the steel-work for decades to come'; the Sun's Solin Hardie: 'For the first time there will be no painters required on the bridge. Job done!'
earliest_attestation: The idiom 'like painting the Forth Bridge' — established by common usage; the ANI report (6 Sept 2011): the phrase 'came into being because of the task of painting the bridge in Scotland, which would start again as soon as the workmen reached the end.'

sources.ref: newcivilengineer.com (9 Dec 2011): painting complete after 10-year, £130m refurbishment; scaffolding removed; no full paint job for at least 20 years; old paint removed by abrasive blasting; triple layer of glass-flake epoxy designed for 25 years, expected to last much longer

newcivilengineer.com (19 Feb 2008): 'The announcement explodes the popular myth that the painting of the 120-year old structure is a job that never ends'; Balfour Beatty £74m contract; glass-flake epoxy designed for at least 20 years, anticipated up to 30

Asian News International via thefreelibrary.com (6 Sept 2011): ~10 years, ~200 workers, 240,000 litres of glass-flake epoxy; 'For the first time there will be no painters required on the bridge. Job done!'; the idiom's origin stated: the job 'would start again as soon as the workmen reached the end'
edinburghlive.co.uk: repeated repainting continued until 2002, when glass-based epoxy was introduced; workers completed the last repainting in 2011; now ~once every 25 years; next due ~2027

edinburghlive.co.uk (21 Jul 2020): the 25-year paint job 'appears to be peeling off just nine years later' — the lifespan claim publicly questioned; carried as the unresolved fence on the 25-year promise, not on the myth

competing_hypotheses: The idiom as idiom (language doesn't die on schedule — the phrase survives in English regardless; only the literal task is dead)

The 25-year promise as a separate claim: in July 2020 the Daily Record/Edinburgh Live photographed peeling paint nine years after the 2011 completion, and the lifespan claim was publicly questioned (Colin Smyth, Scottish Labour) — carried as an unresolved fence, not a grade
falsifiability: Find a continuous repainting cycle on the bridge after December 2011 — the owner-operator's record says there is none: 'no additional full-scale repainting will be needed for at least 20 years.'

title: The '1421' thesis: Zheng He's fleet discovered America
claim: Gavin Menzies' 2002 thesis (1421: The Year China Discovered the World): that during or after Zheng He's sixth voyage, detached Chinese fleets circumnavigated the globe, reached the Americas, Australia, and Antarctica, mapped them, and returned — so China 'discovered' America ~70 years before Columbus and the world ~100 years before Magellan.
place: Beijing (publication/imperial-center anchor of the claim)
grade_reason: The thesis is rejected across the professional literature: Robert Finlay, 'How Not to (Re)Write World History' (Journal of World History, June 2004) demolished the method; Timothy Brook (2019) advises serious readers to avoid Menzies entirely; the '1418 map' star evidence is an 18th-century copy of a European map (Geoff Wade, Asia Research Institute; Sally Church, Cambridge, via LiveScience); no Ming document supports voyages beyond the Indian Ocean; claimed artifacts lack archaeological context.
earliest_attestation: Gavin Menzies, 1421: The Year China Discovered the World (London: Bantam, 2002)

sources.ref: Robert Finlay, 'How Not to (Re)Write World History: Gavin Menzies and the Chinese Discovery of America', Journal of World History, June 2004
Geoff Wade, '1421 And All That' (H-Asia exchange, June 2006) — 'not one single piece of recognised evidence'
Timothy Brook (2019) — 'Serious readers are advised to avoid anything written by Gavin Menzies'
Sally K. Church (Cambridge) and Geoff Wade on the '1418 map': an 18th-century copy of a European map (LiveScience reporting)

competing_hypotheses: The voyages' documented scope is itself the replacement: the fleets reached the east coast of Africa, which is already the most far-reaching documented maritime program of its century — no global circumnavigation is needed to make them remarkable

The popular middle position ('we can't be sure either way') fails the evidence test: a 30,000-man fleet leaves records, wrecks, artifacts, and port-state notices across the ports it touches, and none exist outside the attested Indian Ocean circuit
falsifiability: A Ming-dynasty document, inscription, shipwreck, or excavated artifact context placing a Zheng He fleet in the Atlantic or Pacific (or the Americas) would reopen it; Menzies' 'evidence' is repeatedly shown to be misdated, misread, or contextless — and the bar he would need (fleet-scale traces) is a standard his own case set, not an invention of his critics

title: The Sarajevo Sandwich Myth (the lunch-hour coincidence)
claim: The telling that Gavrilo Princip only happened to be standing outside Moritz Schiller's delicatessen because he had stepped in to buy a sandwich — and that the Archduke's car stopped right in front of him by outrageous coincidence, so that 'no sandwich, no shooting; no shooting, no war.'
place: Sarajevo — Moritz Schiller's delicatessen, Franz Josef Street
grade_reason: Four independent kills: (1) the trial record — neither Princip nor any witness ever mentions eating; (2) the route — Schiller's stood on the original planned motorcade route, so Princip was stationed where he should have been, not where luck put him; (3) the clock — ~10:55 a.m., early for lunch; (4) the provenance — no telling predates the 2003 documentary, and the sandwich is not a 1914 Bosnian menu item (Serbian readers: it would have been burek or pljeskavica).
earliest_attestation: Lion TV 'Days That Shook the World' (2003), at 5:15: 'Gavrilo Princip has just eaten a sandwich, and is now standing outside Schiller's delicatessen ... Completely by chance, fate has brought the assassin and his target within 10 feet of each other.'

title: The Semmelweis 'persecuted martyr' narrative (popular version)
claim: The popular 'persecuted martyr' narrative — that Ignaz Semmelweis was mocked and ridiculed by a closed medical establishment that refused to look at his evidence, and that he was driven into an asylum and to his death by their persecution — is an exaggeration of the real record, largely assembled by later popularizers (notably Nuland's The Doctor's Plague, 2003).
place: Vienna (the historiographic claim's origin point)
grade_reason: The martyrdom narrative is falsified point by point by the contemporary record: the discovery was circulated contemporaneously (Hebra 1847-48, Routh 1848); the Vienna clinic kept the chlorine washings while he was there; Semmelweis himself published almost nothing for fourteen years and his 1861 book's open letters called critics murderers; modern historians (Carter & Carter 2005; Loudon) attribute the slow acceptance to a missing germ-theory mechanism, weak publication, polemics, and politics — not a conspiracy of ridicule.
earliest_attestation: Popular retellings; Nuland, S. B. — The Doctor's Plague (2003) as the modern martyr-narrative's chief popularizer.

sources.ref: Carter, K. C. & Carter, B. R. — Childbed Fever: A Scientific Biography of Ignaz Semmelweis (2005)
Nuland, S. B. — The Doctor's Plague (2003) — the popular martyr narrative's chief modern popularizer
NY Review of Books, 'The Fool of Pest' (2004) — review of Nuland; notes Semmelweis left publication to colleagues, Hebra published Dec 1847/Apr 1848, Routh reported 1848
Springer Medizin, 'Ignac Semmelweis — Father of Hand Hygiene' — mortality drop to ~2.4% after one year of chlorine handwashing
evt-semmelweis-handwashing-1847-001 (VERIFIED) and evt-semmelweis-rejection-001 (CORROBORATED) — the two records this myth distorts

competing_hypotheses: The grain of truth: he was professionally damaged — see evt-semmelweis-rejection-001 CORROBORATED — and the establishment was slow; slowness plus plural causes is not persecution
Minority defense of the martyr reading: the institutional resistance was real and the beatings allegation (1865) may have substance — the death's exact circumstances remain contested
falsifiability: Contemporary documentary proof of an organized campaign of mockery — ridicule as policy — or that the discovery was systematically suppressed rather than widely circulated

title: ABC News 2004 poll: 64% say Moses parted the Red Sea 'literally true word-for-word'
claim: In an ABC News poll of 1,011 American adults (Feb 6-10, 2004), 64% said the story of Moses parting the Red Sea was 'literally true, meaning it happened that way word-for-word'; about 30% said the Bible stories are meant as lessons, not to be taken literally.

grade_reason: The belief is attested by the pollster's own release via consistent secondary reporting; the record grades the attestation of the belief, never the fact.

title: Ingredient delivery: returned asteroid/comet samples contain life's building blocks
claim: Pristine samples returned from carbonaceous asteroids and a comet contain the molecular building blocks of life — amino acids, nucleobases, sugars, phosphate — demonstrating that the ingredients were widespread in the early solar system before life existed on Earth. Delivery of ingredients is demonstrated; the mechanism of life's origin is not.
place: NASA Johnson Space Center, Houston (Bennu sample curation); JAXA Sagamihara (Ryugu)
grade_reason: Three independent sample-return programs (Stardust, Hayabusa2, OSIRIS-REx) with peer-reviewed laboratory analyses converge: the building blocks were present in small bodies before Earth had life. Contamination is controlled by pristine curation, unlike meteorite finds.
earliest_attestation: Stardust capsule return, January 2006; glycine in Wild 2 aerogel reported by Elsila et al. 2009

sources.ref: Elsila et al. 2009, Meteoritics & Planetary Science — glycine in Stardust Wild 2 samples (first amino acid recovered beyond the Moon)
Naraoka et al. 2023, Science — soluble organic molecules including amino acids in Hayabusa2 Ryugu samples
Glavin et al. 2025, Nature Astronomy — 14 of 20 protein amino acids, all five nucleobases, ammonia in OSIRIS-REx Bennu samples; amino acids racemic (~equal L/D)
McCoy et al. 2025, Nature — brine evaporite minerals (sodium carbonates, phosphates) in Bennu samples; parent-body salty water

Furukawa et al. 2026, Nature Geoscience (13 Jul 2026) — ribose, glucose, lyxose, xylose, arabinose, galactose in pristine Bennu material; with nucleobases + phosphate, every chemical component needed to build RNA present in one asteroid's material

Connolly et al. 2026, Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta (in press, DOI 10.1016/j.gca.2026.10.003) — Bennu vs Ryugu organics compared: divergent parent-body histories; Ryugu CI1-like with depleted soluble organics, Bennu heterogeneous with multiple alteration episodes
NASA OSIRIS-REx mission record: 121.6 g returned September 2023; pristine curation at Johnson Space Center

Drozdovskaya et al., COMPASS project, ALMA, 7 papers in A&A October 2026 issue — methanol (the most abundant complex organic molecule in interstellar space) and methanol masers detected in planet-forming disks around >half of 11 young low-mass protostars; deuterated methanol in IRAS 4A2 (Perseus, ~1,000 ly) — prebiotic inventory assembled DURING star/planet formation, not only delivered later: the inheritance-before-delivery line; strengthens the delivery competing hypothesis's premise (pantry was stocked early) without touching the mechanism gap

Connolly et al. 2026, Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta (in press, 6 Oct 2026 listing, doi:10.1016/j.gca.2026.10.003) — 'Prebiotic organic compounds in asteroid Bennu and Ryugu reflect divergent parent body histories': pyrolysis, thermochemolysis, and one-pot derivatization GC-triple-quadrupole-MS of a Ryugu aggregate vs Bennu — Ryugu is CI1-like (increased alkylation of insoluble organics, depleted soluble organics; only tentative β-alanine and 2,4-diaminopyrimidine), Bennu heterogeneous with 14 proteinogenic α-amino acids and five canonical nucleobases by the same technique; the peer-reviewed publication of the divergent-parent-bodies line already on this record (Turin-shroud precedent: context strengthened, grade not). Ingredients delivered; the chemistry-to-cell sequence still unknown

Matsumoto et al. 2026, Nature Astronomy (27 Aug 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41550-026-02962-y) — 'Evolution of ammonia, ammonium and C≡N-bearing species in Ryugu samples': three nitrogen reservoirs mapped in two Ryugu grains (N K-edge XAS/X-ray/IR spectroscopy + electron microscopy) — ammonium in saponite clay (405.6 eV), C≡N-bearing species (399.8 eV), sodium nitrate crystals, all clustered with sodium-carbonate-rich material from the final-stage aqueous alteration (freezing/evaporation concentrating brines over millions of years); independent echo: OSIRIS-REx Bennu samples show similar ammonium-bearing clays

Nature Astronomy Oct 2026 - interstellar erythrulose in G+0.693-0.027 (evt-interstellar-erythrulose-2026-001, CORROBORATED): the delivery pillar's deep-time extension - sugar chemistry predates planetary systems; ingredients, not life

competing_hypotheses: Endogenous synthesis dominated: Earth's own chemistry made most organics; delivery was a minor supplement
Delivery dominated: exogenous organics seeded the prebiotic inventory (still requires an origin mechanism on Earth)
Contamination critique: some detections reflect terrestrial contamination — addressed by pristine sample handling, but the control argument must be re-won per analysis
falsifiability: Demonstrated terrestrial contamination across all three independent sample sets, or a flux model showing delivered organics were negligible against endogenous production

title: The Ark-Encounter/Creation-Museum-exhibit-as-evidence telling (dino-human coexistence)
claim: The dioramas, animatronics, and placards at Answers in Genesis's Creation Museum (Petersburg, KY) and Ark Encounter (Grant County, KY) — the 'dragons were dinosaurs' exhibit, dinosaur animatronics in cages, dinosaurs standing with Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden, dinosaurs aboard the Ark — constitute historical evidence that humans and non-avian dinosaurs lived at the same time. FALSE: a diorama is a claim in three dimensions, and the claim it makes is the young-earth telling — Day-6 creation, juveniles on the Ark, post-Flood climate extinction — which the evidence record (evt-dino-human-coexistence-001, DEBUNKED; evt-paluxy-mantracks-001, DEBUNKED) already kills. The exhibits are the 292nd DEBUNKED family: the museum-exhibit-as-evidence telling.
place: Ark Encounter, Grant County, Kentucky, USA
grade_reason: The telling dies on provenance: the exhibits are the claimant's own staging, not an independent witness. The Paluxy 'man tracks' — the one exhibit-adjacent claim that once had a physical anchor — were autopsied in the field (Kuban) and partially retracted by their own side (Morris 1986, ICR); the remaining displays rest on nothing the museums dug up. DEBUNKED as evidence; the attractions themselves are graded as real public events (the 1.5M-visitor figure is the ministry's own claim, fenced). The Catholic Church's 2014 position (Francis to the Pontifical Academy: evolution does not conflict with Creation) is carried as competing context — the telling is a young-earth sectarian reading, not the Christian consensus.
earliest_attestation: The Creation Museum and Ark Encounter coexistence exhibits themselves (2007–present); documented in the July 2026 Cincinnati Enquirer 10-year anniversary coverage (cincinnati.com, 10 July 2026)

sources.ref: Cincinnati Enquirer, 'Ark Encounter celebrates 10 years marked by a flood of tourists, controversy,' 10 July 2026 — dinosaur animatronics in cages 'because the ministry believes dinosaurs (including carnivorous dinosaurs) were alive at the same time as humans'; Bill Nye: 'a monument dedicated to anti-science'

cajunlimeys.com, 'Summer '26 Trek: Day 21: The Creation Museum,' 1 Aug 2026 — the museum's 'dragons' exhibit ('a movie attempted to explain the link between mythical dragons and dinosaurs'); 'a key point of the Young Earth Creation argument is that dinosaurs were created on the sixth day and coexisted with man'; 'The presence of dinosaurs with man was a prevalent theme'

worldeventsandthebible.com, Ark Encounter visit (~Sept 2026) — 'a picture of Adam and Eve standing in the water with Dinosaurs off in the distance'; 'There is no Biblical or historical documentation to support such a belief'

citizendailypost.com FAQ, October 2026 — 'the Creation Museum and Ark Encounter both show dinosaurs and humans living alongside each other'; 'This is contrary to the scientific consensus that non-avian dinosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago, long before humans appeared'

competing_hypotheses: The exhibits are religious art, not evidence claims — the counter-reading. The record rejects it as a defense of the specific coexistence displays, because the museums themselves present them as evidence of coexistence (the Day-6/dragons/Ark placards are explanatory, not decorative); the art-reading holds only for the scenery, not the signage
The 'birds are dinosaurs' hedge — true and grade-neutral, and not what the exhibits are about (the exhibits show sauropods and theropods with people, not sparrows)
falsifiability: A single fossil of a human in undisturbed Mesozoic strata (the record's standing falsifiability line) — the exhibits cannot supply it, because they are not excavations.

title: Venona 'vindicates' McCarthy
claim: The Venona decrypts prove Senator Joseph McCarthy's accusations were right — that the evidence shows he was justified in his zeal in exposing those he believed to be Soviet spies or communist sympathizers (the form in which the Texas State Board of Education proposed revising high school history curricula in 2009).
place: Austin, Texas (Texas State Board of Education, 2009)
grade_reason: Killed by the scholars who built the case: Klehr himself documents that most of McCarthy's targets are not in the Venona content and the accusations remain largely unsupported by evidence, and Haynes & Klehr state flatly that Venona gives 'no basis' for McCarthy's signature conspiracy charges (Acheson, Marshall).
earliest_attestation: Texas State Board of Education curriculum revision proposal, 2009, as reported in the press; the vindication argument's circulation in the 1990s–2000s after the 1995 release

sources.ref: Wikipedia, 'Venona project' (citing TFN Insider, 29 Oct 2009, 'Rehabilitating Joseph McCarthy?'): 2009 Texas textbook policy suggested 'Venona evidence shows Senator Joseph McCarthy to have been justified in his zeal in exposing those whom he believed to be Soviet spies or communist sympathizers'; historian Harvey Klehr rebuts — 'most people and organizations identified by McCarthy as possible Soviet assets or sympathizers, such as those brought forward in the Army-McCarthy hearings or rival politicians in the Democratic Party, were not mentioned in the Venona content and that his accusations remain largely unsupported by evidence'

Haynes & Klehr, 'Venona: Decoding Soviet Espionage in America' (Yale, 1999), Ch. 1: 'There is no basis in Venona for implicating Acheson or Marshall in a Communist conspiracy, but because the deciphered Venona messages were classified and unknown to the public, demagogues such as McCarthy had the opportunity to mix together accurate information about betrayal by men such as Harry White and Alger Hiss with falsehoods about Acheson and Marshall that served partisan political goals'

competing_hypotheses: The revisionist reading that McCarthy 'in general' was right about espionage even if wrong about individuals — a political judgment, not the evidential claim graded here
The position that Venona's secrecy caused McCarthyism's excesses (the Moynihan Commission view) — compatible with the DEBUNKED grade on vindication
falsifiability: A systematic mapping showing that a substantial share of McCarthy's named targets appear in the Venona decrypts as Soviet assets; Klehr's audit finds the opposite

title: Pew 2010: 72% identify Moses as the Exodus leader; the non-religious know the most
claim: In Pew Research Center's U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey (fielded May 19-June 6, 2010, among 3,412 U.S. adults by landline and cell phone, in English and Spanish), 72% correctly identified Moses — not Job, Elijah, or Abraham — as the biblical figure who led the exodus from Egypt. On the survey's full 32 questions the national average was 16 correct; atheists and agnostics averaged 20.9, Jews 20.5, and Mormons 20.3 — the highest-scoring groups included people with no religious affiliation, while Protestants as a whole averaged 16 and Catholics 14.7.
place: United States (national poll)
grade_reason: The finding is attested by the pollster's own published topline and report with methodology disclosed (n=3,412, dual-frame, oversamples); the record grades the attestation of the survey result, never the event it asks about.
earliest_attestation: Pew Research Center, 'U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey,' Sept 28, 2010 (topline Q.47c: Job 2 / Elijah 3 / Moses 72 / Abraham 5 / Don't know 18)

sources.ref: Pew Research Center, 'New Pew Forum on Religion & Public Life Survey Explores Religious Knowledge in the U.S.,' press release Sept 28, 2010 (the pollster's own release: 16/32 national average; atheists/agnostics 20.9; Jews 20.5; Mormons 20.3; field May 19-June 6, 2010, n=3,412)
Pew Research Center, 'U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey' topline (assets.pewresearch.org — religious-knowledge-topline.pdf; Q.47c: Job 2, Elijah 3, Moses 72, Abraham 5, Don't know 18)

Pew Research Center, 'U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey — Who Knows What About Religion,' Sept 28, 2010 report chapter (the Moses passage: 'more than seven-in-ten Americans (72%) know he was the biblical figure who led the exodus out of Egypt'; sub-group splits: Mormons 92%, Jews and atheists/agnostics ~92%, white evangelicals ~80%, white mainline ~68%, Catholics ~65%)

Pew Research Center, 'What Americans Know About Religion,' July 2019 (follow-up wave: roughly eight-in-ten (79%) identify Moses vs Daniel/Elijah/Joseph; different instrument — carried as a related reading, not a re-measurement)

competing_hypotheses: The Moses question was multiple-choice (options read aloud in random order), so the 72% is recognition, not unaided recall — a harder open-ended format would likely have scored lower
Pew's own overview cautions the 32 questions are not necessarily the most important things to know about religion — the survey measures what it measures, not 'religious literacy' in full
The 2019 follow-up wave ('What Americans Know About Religion') asked a differently-worded Moses question with different options (79% correct), so the two waves are not a strict trend line
falsifiability: Release of Pew's topline or dataset contradicting the 72% figure, or the pollster retracting the finding.

title: Pew religious-knowledge quiz: the 2010 telephone wave vs the 2019 online wave — the inversion survived the mode change
claim: Between Pew Research Center's two U.S. religious-knowledge surveys, the survey mode changed completely. The 2010 wave ('U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey,' report Sept 28, 2010) was interviewer-administered by telephone — dual-frame landline + cell random-digit dial, n=3,412 U.S. adults, fielded May 19–June 6, 2010, in English and Spanish. The 2019 wave ('What Americans Know About Religion,' report July 23, 2019) was self-administered online — fielded Feb 4–19, 2019, n=10,971, mostly on Pew's American Trends Panel (10,429 panelists, probability-recruited online) plus 542 Ipsos KnowledgePanel oversample interviews (Jewish, Mormon, Hispanic Protestant subgroups), margin of sampling error ±1.5 points. The headline finding — the religiously unaffiliated outscoring the affiliated — survived the crossing: 2010 (telephone): atheists/agnostics 20.9 of 32, general public 16, Protestants 16, Catholics 14.7. 2019 (online): Jews 18.7, atheists 17.9, agnostics 17.0, general public 14.2. The group-ranking pattern held after demographic controls in both waves. The inversion is mode-robust: it was not an artifact of interviewer administration, and it did not vanish under self-administration.
place: United States (national polls)
grade_reason: The mode facts are attested by the pollster's own published methodology sections in both reports (primary documents); the inversion's survival is read off the published group-score tables, not inferred. Graded as poll-instrument attestation, never as a claim about religion itself.
earliest_attestation: Pew Research Center, 'U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey,' Sept 28, 2010 (methodology: dual-frame RDD telephone) and 'What Americans Know About Religion,' July 23, 2019 (methodology: survey conducted online Feb. 4–19, 2019, among 10,971 respondents, mostly American Trends Panel)

sources.ref: Pew Research Center, 'U.S. Religious Knowledge Survey,' Sept 28, 2010 — methodology: telephone interviews, dual-frame landline + cell RDD, n=3,412, May 19–June 6, 2010, English and Spanish; topline Q.47c Moses 72%

Pew Research Center, 'What Americans Know About Religion' full report, July 23, 2019 — 'a survey conducted online Feb. 4 to 19, 2019, among 10,971 respondents... mostly among members of Pew Research Center's American Trends Panel (a nationally representative panel of randomly selected U.S. adults recruited from landline and cellphone random-digit-dial surveys and an address-based survey), supplemented by interviews with members of the Ipsos KnowledgePanel'; margin ±1.5 pts

Pew Research Center, 'What Americans Know About the Holocaust' methodology markdown, Jan 22, 2020 — confirms the pair: '(The first was conducted in 2010.) This time... 10,429 were members of Pew's American Trends Panel (ATP), an online survey panel'

competing_hypotheses: The two quizzes did not use identical question sets (32 questions each, overlapping but not the same items), so the comparison is of the group-ranking pattern, not of item-level scores — the ranking survived, not the numbers

Online self-administration changes the answering psychology in both directions: less social-desirability pressure on some items, but no interviewer to clarify confusion and new hazards (speeders, straight-liners) — the literature's net-direction verdict is mixed, so 'mode-robust' is a finding about this result, not a law

The Moses recognition question itself was reworded between waves (72% correct in 2010 vs 79% in 2019 with different options) — the two waves are not a strict trend line (already carried on evt-pew-2010-religious-knowledge-001)
falsifiability: A Pew-published mode experiment showing the 2019 group rankings are an artifact of the online mode, or retraction/correction of either report's methodology section.

title: Wind setdown as a physical crossing mechanism (Drews & Han 2010)
claim: Wind setdown — a sustained strong wind driving water back — can physically expose dry passage in shallow Delta waters: Drews & Han (2010, PLoS ONE) modeled a 28 m/s (63 mph) easterly wind for 12 hours opening a 3-4 km long, 5 km wide mudflat for about 4 hours at the reconstructed Lake of Tanis / Pelusiac branch, with the water standing as barriers on both sides of the exposed flats.
place: Lake of Tanis / Pelusiac branch reconstruction (eastern Nile Delta)
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed hydrodynamic modeling confirms the mechanism is physically possible — which proves the mechanism, never the event; the timeline keeps those two claims on separate records.
earliest_attestation: Drews & Han (2010), 'Dynamics of Wind Setdown at Suez and the Eastern Nile Delta,' PLoS ONE 5(8): e12481 — building on Nof & Paldor's earlier wind-setdown modeling and Volzinger & Androsov's 2004 reef study.

sources.ref: Drews C, Han W (2010), PLoS ONE 5(8): e12481 (peer-reviewed ocean-model study; satellite + bathymetric reconstruction)
Volzinger & Androsov (2004), Bulletin of the Russian Academy of Sciences (Suez-reef wind-setdown model; Drews & Han later showed a non-uniform reef retains unwadeable channels)
Nof & Paldor (earlier wind-setdown work on the Gulf of Suez)

Critical counter-reading: the tsunami-modeling paper (MDPI J. Marine Sci. Eng. 2015) notes the Tanis scenario depends on a hypothetical reconstructed topography and fits the Exodus itinerary poorly on Hoffmeier's own geography

competing_hypotheses: A wind-setdown event lies behind a theologized crossing account (mechanism-true, narrative-amplified)
The mechanism is irrelevant: the narrative is a literary composition with no natural event behind it
The Drews & Han reconstructed bathymetry is itself contested — kill the topography and the specific scenario falls
falsifiability: Proof that the reconstructed Tanis/Pelusiac bathymetry is wrong would kill the specific scenario (not wind setdown generally); wind setdown is ordinary fluid mechanics and survives regardless.

title: El Azizia's 136°F record decertified (2012)
claim: The 136.4°F (58°C) temperature recorded at El Azizia, Libya, on 13 September 1922 — the long-standing world heat record — was formally decertified by the World Meteorological Organization in 2012 after a committee investigation found it invalid.
place: El Azizia, Libya
grade_reason: Multiple independent accounts agree: Christopher Burt's investigation prompted a 13-climatologist WMO committee (including Burt and Randall Cerveny); after a year-long investigation the committee identified five major concerns — problematical instrumentation, a probable new and inexperienced observer, unrepresentative microclimate, poor correspondence to other locations, poor comparison to subsequent values — and the WMO World Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes rejected the 58°C reading, promoting Death Valley's 134°F to the official record.
earliest_attestation: The WMO committee report and September 2012 announcement

sources.ref: Smithsonian Magazine: the WMO committee 'identified five major concerns with the 1922 El Azizia temperature extreme record, specifically (a) potentially problematical instrumentation, (b) a probable new and inexperienced observer at time of observation, (c) unrepresentative microclimate of the observation site, (d) poor correspondence of the extreme to other locations and (e) poor comparison to subsequent temperature values recorded at the site. Based on these concerns, the WMO World Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes has rejected this temperature extreme of 58°C as the highest temperature officially recorded on the planet.'

UPI via Space Daily (Dec 2012): 'The U.N. climate agency has changed the world's hottest day on record from Sept. 13, 1922, in Libya, to July 10, 1913, in California's Death Valley.' Burt: 'The more we looked at it, the more obvious it appeared to be an error.' The committee of 13 climatologists investigated for a year.

falsifiability: WMO archive records showing the El Azizia reading still listed as the world record

title: The 2012 Mayan 'end of the world' — debunked
claim: The Mayan calendar predicted the end of the world on 21 December 2012.
place: Tortuguero, Tabasco, Mexico (site of Monument 6 — heavily quarried/damaged before its significance was recognized)
grade_reason: The only ancient reference (Tortuguero Monument 6) is eroded and describes an investiture ceremony of the deity Bolon Yokte', not an apocalypse; the Long Count is an odometer that rolls over; other inscriptions project dates to ~4772 CE; contemporary Maya leaders and Mexico's INAH publicly rejected the apocalyptic reading as a Western distortion.
earliest_attestation: Modern phenomenon: the apocalyptic reading is a 20th–21st-century Western construction (Jenkins 1987; the film '2012' 2009); the only Classic-period reference is Tortuguero Monument 6, 7th century CE

sources.ref: Tortuguero Monument 6 (Tabasco; ruler Bahlam Ajaw 'Jaguar Lord', early 7th c. CE) — the only Classic-period reference to 13.0.0.0.0; stone cracked and eroded, end of passage near-illegible

Gronemeyer, Sven & MacLeod, Barbara — 'What Could Happen in 2012: A Re-Analysis of the 13-Bak'tun Prophecy on Tortuguero Monument 6' (Wayeb Notes 34, 2010): the text describes the 'display'/'investiture' of Bolon Yokte' — a ceremony, not an apocalypse

Archaeology Magazine, Nov/Dec 2012 — 'The Maya Sense of Time': of ~5,000 known Maya inscriptions, only two (Tortuguero, Comalcalco) reference the 2012 date; the Palenque Temple of the Inscriptions projects dates to ~4772 CE

Mexico's INAH, Nov 2011 (AP): 'western messianic thought has twisted the cosmovision of ancient civilizations like the Maya' — the institute convened 60 Maya experts at Palenque to dispel the doomsday reading
Oxlaljuj Ajpop / Felipe Gomez (AFP, Oct 2012): Guatemala's Maya alliance publicly protested the twisting of their traditions for doomsday tourism

Reuters/Ipsos Global Public Affairs poll, May 2012 (n=16,262, 21 countries): 10% believed the Mayan calendar could signify the end of the world in 2012; ~15% believed the world would end in their lifetime — carried as belief data, not evidence

competing_hypotheses: Jenkins-style esoteric reading: the 2012 date marks an alignment with the galactic center — no Maya text supports this; it is a modern synthesis of unrelated ideas
The misreading was partly honest: 'end of a cycle' reads to a non-Maya reader like 'end of time' — the popular claim is the mistranslation of a rollover, not a fabrication from nothing
falsifiability: A Maya inscription explicitly describing destruction, cataclysm, or a final ending at 13.0.0.0.0 would reopen it; no such text exists among ~5,000 known inscriptions

title: The Denisovan EPAS1 haplotype and Tibetan altitude adaptation
claim: Huerta-Sanchez et al. 2014 (Nature, doi 10.1038/nature13408): Tibetans carry a Denisovan-derived EPAS1 haplotype at ~80-87% frequency, conferring efficient blood-oxygen response to hypoxia without the heart-straining side effects of other high-altitude adaptations — the clearest case of adaptive archaic introgression.
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed; haplotype frequency and Denisovan phylogeny replicated across studies
earliest_attestation: Huerta-Sanchez et al., Nature 2014
competing_hypotheses: None serious; the Denisovan origin of the haplotype is established by phylogeny
falsifiability: Denser archaic sampling could reassign the haplotype's source lineage

title: Erebus (2014) and Terror (2016) - the wrecks, found where the testimony said
claim: Both Franklin expedition wrecks were found in the 2010s at Inuit-indicated locations. HMS Erebus was located in September 2014 in the Queen Maud Gulf, northeast of O'Reilly Island (Wilfrid Laurier area) - 'near to where Inukpujijuk told Hall it had sunk' (Parks Canada), after six years of sonar searching guided by Inuit oral history and Louie Kamookak's consultations; the find followed a Government of Nunavut team's recovery of cached Erebus artefacts from an island. HMS Terror was located in September 2016 in Terror Bay, about 60 miles north of Erebus, by the Arctic Research Foundation's vessel Martin Bergmann - after Inuk crewmember Sammy Kogvik reported having seen a mast-like object in the Terror Bay ice six years earlier; Parks Canada confirmed the wreck resting upright in about 24 metres of water in remarkably preserved condition. falsifiability: A peer-reviewed excavation report placing the lintel in primary stratigraphic context and confirming the Mesen reading would settle the identification; attribution of the lintel to a different find-spot would falsify it.

title: The 2026 'Tell El-Kharouba fortress proves the Exodus' telling
claim: In October 2026 press coverage (e.g. Fox News Digital), the Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities' October 11, 2026 announcement of a 3,000-year-old New Kingdom fortress at Tell El-Kharouba (Sheikh Zuweid, North Sinai, on the Horus Military Road; Thutmose I cartouche on a jar handle) was framed as fresh archaeological evidence supporting the Exodus narrative — with press explicitly invoking Exod 13:17's 'way of the land of the Philistines'.
place: Tell El-Kharouba, Sheikh Zuweid, North Sinai
grade_reason: The telling grades DEBUNKED as a telling: a New Kingdom Egyptian fortress on the Horus Military Road is precisely what the 'empty Sinai / Egyptian-territory Canaan' fence of evt-exodus-literalist-reading-001 predicts — Egyptian military infrastructure east of the Delta is evidence of Egyptian control, not of an escaping slave multitude of 600,000 men. The press frame overreads an Egyptian fortress into an Israelite-exodus proof; the find's content points the other way.
earliest_attestation: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announcement, October 11, 2026

sources.ref: Egyptian Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities announcement (October 11, 2026): 3,000-year-old New Kingdom fortress at Tell El-Kharouba, Sheikh Zuweid, North Sinai — on the Horus Military Road; Thutmose I jar handle
Fox News Digital October 2026 coverage of the Tell El-Kharouba discovery, framing it in relation to the Exodus route (Exod 13:17 'way of the land of the Philistines')
evt-mesen-exodus-telling-2026-001 (the Tell Abu Seifi/Mesen lintel press telling — same 'fortress proves Exodus' pattern, DEBUNKED)

competing_hypotheses: The fortress's position on the military road corroborates the general geography of Exodus 13:17 as a known route
The press framing is venue-driven (Exodus angle draws readers) and carries no archaeological claim of its own
falsifiability: A peer-reviewed publication of the fortress linking its occupation layers, inscriptions, or associated finds to an Israelite population movement — rather than Egyptian military logistics — would reopen the record.

title: The 2026 ERC 'Tracing Scribes and Scrolls' project — a materials database for the Dead Sea Scrolls
claim: In 2026 the European Research Council awarded a five-year grant of 2.5 million euros to Mladen Popović (University of Groningen), with the Israel Antiquities Authority and European laboratories, for the project 'Tracing Scribes and Scrolls': the first large-scale 'chemical signature' database of the Dead Sea Scrolls — parchment composition, collagen, processing residues, inks, organic substances — combined with palaeography, codicology and artificial intelligence, to reconstruct where the manuscripts were produced (their provenance), not just where they were hidden.
place: University of Groningen (project lead); Israel Antiquities Authority, Jerusalem (collaborator)
grade_reason: The grant award and the project's stated scope are documented facts of 2026; the findings it will produce are future and do not move any manuscript grade.
earliest_attestation: ERC grant announcement and project launch materials, 2026.

sources.ref: ZENIT, 'AI and materials analysis offer new insights into the Qumran scrolls' (18 Aug 2026) — the ERC grant, €2.5M, Popović/Groningen, IAA collaboration, chemical-signature database

competing_hypotheses: The project's premise — that materials analysis can assign scrolls to production centers — will succeed and revise the Qumran-community authorship model
The premise will confirm the existing palaeographic picture: chemistry tracks preparation practice, which may not map cleanly onto place
That provenance is recoverable at all for manuscripts whose production histories are two millennia old — the database may document difference without resolving origin
falsifiability: If the ERC award record is inaccurate; the record makes no claim about findings, so no finding can falsify it.

title: TELLING (DEBUNKED): Isaiah's Hebrew says 'virgin'
claim: The telling under test: 'Isaiah's Hebrew text prophesied that a virgin would conceive' — i.e., the original Hebrew of Isaiah 7:14 says 'virgin.'
place: Jerusalem (the oracle's setting; the telling is modern and placeless)
grade_reason: The Hebrew reads ha-almah ('the young woman') in the Masoretic Text and in 1QIsaa (2nd c. BCE); 'virgin' (parthenos) is the Septuagint's Greek choice, quoted by Matthew 1:23. The telling attributes the Greek to the Hebrew.
earliest_attestation: The telling circulates in popular preaching and apologetics; the refutation is the Hebrew text (MT, 1QIsaa) against the LXX

sources.ref: evt-isaiah-almah-parthenos-001 — the fork documented (parent record)
1QIsaa reads 'lmh; Aquila/Symmachus/Theodotion read neanis — the Hebrew and the revised Greek agree against parthenos

competing_hypotheses: The Christian doctrinal reading via the Greek is fenced as theology, not graded here: the claim under test is strictly about what the Hebrew says
Almah's semantic range may include virginity in context (Walton) — but range is not denotation, and the LXX's own sibling translators (Aquila, Symmachus, Theodotion) chose neanis
falsifiability: A Hebrew witness to Isaiah 7:14 reading betulah, or a demonstrated pre-Christian Hebrew semantic consensus that almah denotes virginity

title: American miracle-experience belief, 2026 (belief-ledger)
claim: A 2026 nationally representative American survey (Wheatley Institute at BYU, Survey of Lived Religion, n=2,005 adults via Qualtrics) found about half of Americans say they experience or witness what they consider a miracle at least a few times a year — 10% more than once a week, 9% weekly, 11% once or twice a month, 20% a few times a year; 26% seldom, 24% never. 68% report a spiritual experience, 46% within the previous month. The record grades the BELIEF/EXPERIENCE-ATTESTATION (the poll), never the supernatural character of any reported event.
place: United States (national survey)
grade_reason: A representative national poll on reported experience, multiply reported (beliefnet Sept 2026); grades the belief-attestation (what people say they experience), never the events' supernatural character — the attestation rule applied
earliest_attestation: Wheatley Institute (Brigham Young University) Survey of Lived Religion, nationally representative sample of 2,005 American adults, self-weighted with quotas across Protestants/Catholics/general Christians/religious minorities/nones; reported September 2026

sources.ref: 'Half of Americans Say They Witness Miracles Several Times a Year, Study Finds' (beliefnet.com, Sept 2026): Wheatley Institute Survey of Lived Religion, 2,005 adults — ~50% experience/witness a miracle at least a few times a year (10% more than weekly, 9% weekly, 11% monthly, 20% few-times-a-year); 76% at least seldom; 24% never; 68% spiritual experience, 46% within last month; researchers: 'American religion is changing, not disappearing'

competing_hypotheses: Experiences counted as 'miracles' are unexplained-then or culturally framed ordinary events — a belief phenomenon, which is exactly what the attestation rule grades
Wording effects: the survey asks what respondents 'consider to be a miracle,' so the finding is about classification habits, not event frequencies
falsifiability: An independent representative American survey finding substantially different figures, or a published methodological audit showing the sample was unrepresentative, would force a re-grade

title: Xujiayao proteome 2026 — the juluensis holotype is molecularly Denisovan
claim: Palaeoproteomics (LC-MS/MS) on two Xujiayao Middle Pleistocene specimens (parietal PA1490/XJY-6; mandible ramus PA1497/XJY-14, ~199–138 ka, Nihewan Basin, northern China) recovered 18 endogenous ancient proteins; the Denisovan-specific COL1A2-996K variant was identified in high-quality, deamidation-validated peptides, and a Bayesian phylogeny (2,074 amino-acid positions) places Xujiayao monophyletic with Denisova3 at >99% posterior support — the Xujiayao hominins are molecularly Denisovan.
place: Xujiayao, Nihewan Basin, Hebei Province, China
grade_reason: Peer-reviewed Nature paper with explicit peptide-level evidence (Denisovan-specific variant, deamidation validation, >99% posterior phylogeny) — molecular, not morphological. The two-specimen scope and the morphology-only extension are honestly bounded in the record, which is why the grade stops at CORROBORATED rather than VERIFIED.
earliest_attestation: Xing S., Wu Z., Shao Q., Ge J., Bennett E. A., Rao H., Lin S., Zhao Y., Liu F., Liu Y., Zhou K., Feng X., Jiangzuo Q., & Fu Q. (Fu Qiaomei lab, IVPP Beijing), Nature 21 Oct 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11132-z — the peer-reviewed primary publication

sources.ref: Xing S. et al. (Fu Qiaomei lab, IVPP Beijing), Nature 21 Oct 2026, DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11132-z — 'The proteome of Middle Pleistocene Xujiayao and common Denisovan morphology': 18 endogenous proteins, the Denisovan-specific COL1A2-996K variant, Bayesian monophyly with Denisova3
Nature News, 21 Oct 2026 (d41586-026-03360-0) — 'This is what the mysterious Denisovans looked like'; Fabrice Demeter (Copenhagen): 'a major step forward'; Sally Wasef on the proteomic method
bioengineer.org, 22 Oct 2026 — press echo of the Xujiayao paper (venue, not evidence)

competing_hypotheses: The morphology-only inference: the authors also compare Jinniushan, Dali and Hualongdong cranial morphology (low profile, massive brow, flat zygomaxillary, weak prognathism) and infer they belong to the Denisovan lineage too — but those specimens have NO molecular data; proteomics sampled only two Xujiayao individuals, so that extension is inference, not evidence

The taxonomy fight: Xujiayao is the holotype of Homo juluensis (Wu & Bae 2024); the holotype material is now molecularly Denisovan — a heavy blow to juluensis-as-distinct-species, and under ICZN priority H. longi (2021, Dragon Man — itself molecularly Denisovan) would precede H. juluensis (2024) if any species name is retained; the name question is an institutional decision, not yet made
falsifiability: Re-analysis showing the COL1A2-996K peptides are contamination or modern; a phylogeny placing the Xujiayao proteome outside the Denisovan clade; independent replication failing to recover the Denisovan-specific variants

title: The 'London Zoo was the first zoo' myth
claim: London Zoo (founded 1828) was the world's first zoo.
place: London Zoo, Regent's Park, London (coordinates via map.geocode, FULL_ADDRESS match)
grade_reason: Killed three ways: (1) Tiergarten Schönbrunn, Vienna — founded 1752 as an imperial menagerie, open to the public 1779, still operating — predates London by 76 years and holds the widely accepted 'oldest zoo still in operation' title; (2) the Ménagerie du Jardin des Plantes, Paris — inaugurated 1794 by the National Convention, free and publicly scientific from inception — predates London by 34 years; (3) London Zoo's own institution refuses the unqualified claim, and reputable secondary sources explicitly deny it. The 187th DEBUNKED family on this timeline.
earliest_attestation: None documented as an institutional claim: ZSL's own official history states 'London Zoo is the world's oldest scientific zoo' — never the world's first zoo. A London history piece explicitly writes 'While it wasn't the first zoo in the world (but was the world's first scientific zoo)'.

sources.ref: ZSL — 'London Zoo is the world's oldest scientific zoo' (10 things you may not know about London Zoo)
exploring-london.com — 'While it wasn't the first zoo in the world (but was the world's first scientific zoo)'
Dr. Briony Cates mission pass, 2026-10-14 (research subagent report on file: Schönbrunn 1752, Jardin des Plantes 1794, Tower menagerie c.1204–1835, 'zoo' word origin c.1847)

competing_hypotheses: The claim is sometimes read in its defensible form: London Zoo is the world's oldest scientific zoo — the framing the Zoological Society of London itself uses

What counts as a 'zoo' vs a 'menagerie' is definitional, not factual: if imperial/private menageries count, zoos go back to antiquity (this does not save the unqualified claim, which names London 1828)
No reputable source located makes the unqualified claim; the flat 'first zoo' reading appears to exist only as popular misconception
falsifiability: A reputable institutional or scholarly source actually asserting, unqualified, that the 1828 London Zoo was the world's first zoo — while surviving the existence of the 1752 Schönbrunn menagerie and the 1794 Paris Ménagerie.

title: The Washington wooden-teeth myth
claim: George Washington's dentures were made of wood.
place: Mount Vernon, Virginia (the surviving complete set, Donald W. Reynolds Museum and Education Center)
grade_reason: Killed by the objects themselves: four surviving Washington dentures are built from hippo/walrus/elephant ivory, cow/horse/human teeth, and lead, brass, silver, and gold alloys — zero wood as a tooth material (Mount Vernon FAQ; STAT reporting on the Greenwood 1789 set). The likely mechanism of the myth is documented: stained, grainy ivory (Greenwood's 1798 'very black' letter). The 186th DEBUNKED family on this timeline.
earliest_attestation: None documented: no 18th- or 19th-century source describes Washington wearing wooden dentures. The dentures that survive (Mount Vernon, New York Academy of Medicine, National Museum of Dentistry) contain no wood as a tooth material — only tiny wood pegs used as spacers to hold ivory teeth in place (Mount Vernon Dentures FAQ).

sources.ref: George Washington's Mount Vernon — Washington's Dentures FAQ: 'Collectively, these four dentures include: hippopotamus, walrus, and probably elephant ivory; cow, horse, and human teeth; lead, brass, silver, gold, and tiny wood pegs' (pegs only)

George Washington's Mount Vernon — 'George Washington's Teeth': denture materials list (human teeth; cow, donkey, horse teeth; hippo, walrus, possibly elephant ivory; lead, tin, copper, silver alloys; gold)
John Greenwood to George Washington, 1798: a set described as 'very black', advised regular cleaning — via Poynter fact-check 2026
STAT (Bob Tedeschi, 2017): the New York Academy of Medicine's Greenwood 1789 lower denture — hippo ivory with human teeth; the case inscription documenting Greenwood's making

DVIDS (2022): Mount Vernon senior curator Susan Schoelwer — dentures 'may have looked wooden, particularly after they had been stained, but wood was not used in constructing any of his dental fittings'

competing_hypotheses: The myth arose from the appearance of the dentures: hippopotamus ivory that had stained dark brown and grainy with age (documented in John Greenwood's 1798 letter describing a set as 'very black' and advising more regular cleaning)
The myth predates the modern examination of the surviving dentures and its true origin is undocumented (stated honestly — Poynter 2026: 'We don't know where the wooden teeth myth started')
falsifiability: A contemporary 18th- or 19th-century document (invoice, letter, advertisement) describing wooden dentures made for Washington, or a surviving attributed denture with wooden teeth.
